data.title: Tiny Undervalued Hardware Companions (2024)
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一些实用且便宜的电脑配件，如各种角度转换器、USB适配器、SATA转USB-C/A适配器等，帮助解决日常使用中的小问题。例如，RJ45角度适配器可以避免网线直接垂直伸出笔记本侧面，USB-C和USB-A角度适配器也有类似功能。此外，文章还提到SATA转USB适配器适用于硬盘克隆，USB-C与USB-A互转适配器可应对接口变化，以及小型WiFi或Bluetooth无线适配器方便添加无线功能。这些小工具大多价格低廉（约1-5美元），可在AliExpress等平台找到。尽管文章像是在为AliExpress做推广，但实际并非如此。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各种科技配件和电缆的管理、使用及推荐

不同观点：
• blitzar：怀念曾经苹果的磁性充电器有直角设计，但这种技术似乎已经失传。
• EvanAnderson：认为RJ45双母 coupler（连接适配器）非常实用，尤其是在需要临时接入网络时，可以方便地恢复原状，且在电缆长度不足时可以通过短电缆连接延长使用。
• epakai：喜欢存储各种小适配器，并通过使用多层桌和粘贴式小抽屉来有效组织和存放这些配件，方便快速取用。
• _tom_：使用24格收纳盒来分类存放不同类型的电缆，以避免在大盒子中翻找。
• o11c：提醒大多数USB到SATA适配器不支持硬盘驱动器（HDD），仅支持固态硬盘（SSD），并推荐了一种多功能USB A到C的适配器电缆。
• citizenpaul：购买了Sennheiser HD560S耳机，并通过V-MODA的BoomPro Mic增强了麦克风功能，同时带音量调节的功能让他觉得非常实用。
• wesleyd：使用大型的16口电源条和强力魔术贴来整理桌下设备，并提到使用SATA适配器像磁带机一样备份数据。
• quailfarmer：建议添加便携式HDMI/VGA显示器，以便检查无头机器（headless machines）。
• analog31：推荐长电源线和带长线的插线板，特别适用于避免在某些安装环境中违反安全规定。
• nickphx：不信任AliExpress上的USB-C电缆或转换器，暗示可能存在质量问题。
• rbanffy：建议90度旋转的RJ-45公对公连接器可以方便组建类似RPi的集群。
• 7speter：提到Lightning到USB-C转换器可以让一些较新的iOS设备变成便携电脑，或者用NVMe作为额外存储。

补充讨论：
• 关于USB适配器的争议：o11c指出某些USB-to-SATA适配器不支持HDD，而nickphx则对AliExpress上的USB-C电缆质量表示不信任。
• 关于Ethernet连接的实用性：EvanAnderson和rbanffy都提到了RJ45连接器和适配器的实际应用，包括临时接入网络和组建集群的便利性。
• 关于电缆和适配器的便携性：nicbou和wesleyd强调了使用较短或可伸缩电缆以及便携式适配器在旅行和安装中的优势。
• 关于音频设备的改进：gavinray对带有音量调节功能的BoomPro Mic给予高度评价，认为这种设计应被广泛采用。

44333960.article_content:
After playing/working with computers for more then 25 years I started to appreciate small but handy valuable stuff – like adapters or handlers or … yeah – all kind of stuff. With many of them I did not even knew they existed until I find out about them – mostly accidentally or after long searching for some problem solution. Today I will share them with You – so maybe they will end up handy also for You.
… and while they make my life easier – they are mostly very cheap too.
The
Table of Contents
is below.
RJ45 Angle Adapters
RJ45 Angle Cable Adapters
RJ45 Join Adapters
SATA to USB-C or USB-A Adapters
Angle USB-C and USB-A Adapters
USB-A <=> USB-C Adapters
Tiny USB WiFi or Bluetooth Dongle
USB-C <=> Micro USB Adapter
USB-C <=> Laptops/Routers/5.5mmx2.5mm Adapters
Creative BT-W2 USB-A Bluetooth Adapter
External Microphone for SONY Headphones
Headphones Handle
Dual USB-C and USB-A Pendrive (SanDisk)
Tiny USB-A Hub
Quad USB-C / USB-A / Lightning / Micro USB Adapter with MicroSD Card Slot
Angle Power Adapters
C13/C14 Power Adapters with Additional C1/C2 or C5/C6 Sockets
HDMI 3in1 Switch with Remote Control
Cable Organizers
Mouse Jigger
FM Transmitter
Summary
The whole article can ‘feel’ like a sponsored entry for the
https://aliexpress.com
portal – but it is not – its just the most cheap place I was able to find these gems. Feel free to share even cheaper one if You have one.
~
RJ45 Angle Adapters
I mostly use laptops to do various tasks and cables sticking out on the sides perpendicularly does not help. Not many laptops today have the RJ45 LAN socket – but if they do – they are mostly on the side of the laptop.
Thanks to such angle RJ45 adapters it is no longer a problem.
You can find them for about
$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
page – with the
RJ45 ANGLE ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
RJ45 Angle Cable Adapters
The mentioned earlier
RJ45 Angle Adapters
are quite bulky – but as an alternative its possible to get a short 40cm cable with smaller plug.
Not sure if its noticeable on the picture below – but I also cut the top ‘cover’ with knife of the plug – so its easier to detach.
There are of course all four angles to choose from.
One may also use the end of that 40cm cable-adapter as a ‘stopper’ to not fall inside the desk hole as shown on the image below.
You can find them for about
$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
RJ45 ANGLE ADAPTER CABLE
keywords in their search.
~
RJ45 Join Adapters
Often I found myself in a situation that the currently available LAN cable was too short to reach and it needed a lot of work to plot another – longer one.
With these simple ‘join’ adapters it is no longer a problem. You would not use them in a serious Data Center with 10+ GE speeds – but for home 1.0-2.5 GE speeds its more then enough.
You can find them for about
$1-$2
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
RJ45 JOIN ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
SATA to USB-C or USB-A Adapters
Multiple times I needed to clone some old disk to new SSD – just to make an old system faster.
I usually boot from some USB drive with FreeBSD and while new SSD is attached with these adapters – I then execute
dd(8)
command to clone the old HDD disk to new SSD drive … and then just swap them out.
You can find them for about
$1-$5
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
SATA USB ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
Angle USB-C and USB-A Adapters
As we already talked about RJ45 angle adapters … there are also USB-C and USB-A angle adapters.
The do the same good job with cables to not stick out on a side of a laptop.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
ANGLE USB ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
USB-A <=> USB-C Adapters
In the progressing and always changing world yesterday the USB-A was king and tomorrow the USB-C will be.
There are multiple cases in which you will need these – from simple USB headphones to USB pendrives and other stuff.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
USB-C USB-A ADAPTER
keywords in their search.
~
Tiny USB WiFi or Bluetooth Dongle
Multiple times I have found myself in a situation where it was very convenient to just add some WiFi or Bluetooth chip over USB port and do the job instead of trying to achieve the same without such chips.
While I usually omit Bluetooth I can not say the same about WiFi … and as FreeBSD lacks a little in that department – using a very tiny chip such as
Realtek RTL8188CUS
often does the job done.
You can find them for about
$1-$3
– for example – on
https://aliexpress.com
– with the
WIFI USB
or
BLUETOOTH USB
keywords in their search.
~
USB-C <=> Micro USB Adapter
In the past – in the USB Micro times – I remember using an adapter to be able to charge – then new and uncommon – USB-C devices.

data.title: Learn you Galois fields for great good (2023)
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了有关抽象代数的系列内容，重点讲解伽罗瓦域（有限域）及其在计算机科学中的应用。作者提到，当前缺乏适合计算机科学家的学习资源，多数材料要么过于简化，要么假设读者具备纯数学背景。为此，作者计划通过循序渐进的方式，结合实际代码实现，填补这一空白。抽象代数关注数字间的关系而非数字本身，适用于数据编码、加密、纠错等领域。系列内容从基础理论开始，逐步介绍如Reed-Solomon、AES等应用，包含大量练习以帮助理解。尽管不要求太多数学背景，但某些应用需要线性代数知识。代码将采用Rust编写，注重可读性和教育性，而非性能优化。最终目标是为计算机科学家提供易于理解的参考实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Galois域的构造及其与复数构造的类比，以及对代数教学和学习资源的讨论

不同观点：
• kasadkad认为Galois域的构造与复数的构造类似，通过添加一个“虚拟数”来扩展域，但需要选择不可约多项式以确保构造的有效性。他详细解释了如何通过选择适当的多项式来构造GF(4)，并指出了不同多项式的选择对构造的影响。
• nayuki提供了一些相关的解释资源链接，涵盖了群和域的内容，为读者提供了进一步学习的资料。
• tempodox强调了用简单语言解释复杂概念的重要性，引用了爱因斯坦的名言来支持这一观点。
• __rito__表达了对帖子的赞赏，认为内容精彩。
• JackFr指出了文章中关于域的闭包性质和多项式乘法约简步骤的缺失，提出了改进建议。
• revskill批评了代数教学中只给出定义而不解释原因的做法，认为这不利于学习。
• behnamoh提到文章使用了Rust语言，但个人偏好Haskell或Lean，并希望可视化内容能贯穿整个章节。
• graycat提供了关于抽象代数和Galois理论的经典教材推荐，并分享了个人学习经验，指出了一些在有限域中需要特殊证明的情况。
• gnabgib提供了一个存档链接，可能与讨论内容相关。
• m3kw9对标题的语法错误提出了批评。
• untitled2反驳了对计算机科学课程中缺少代数内容的抱怨，认为每所大学都提供数学作为辅修课程，质疑那些没有选择数学辅修的人的职业选择。

补充讨论：
• kasadkad的评论引发了对如何选择适当多项式来构造Galois域的深入讨论，并与复数的构造进行了类比。
• 不同读者对文章的细节和表达方式提出了不同看法，如JackFr对内容不完整的批评和tempodox对简单语言的强调。
• behnamoh和graycat的评论扩展了讨论范围，涉及编程语言偏好和经典教材推荐，丰富了学习资源的选择。
• untitled2对代数在计算机科学课程中的地位提出了不同的看法，引发了对课程设置的争议。

争议焦点：
• 代数教学中是否充分解释了定义的根源问题（revskill的观点）。
• 计算机科学课程中代数内容的设置是否合理（untitled2的观点）。
• 文章内容的完整性和表达方式是否足够清晰（JackFr和m3kw9的批评）。

Introduction
This is the introduction to a series on Abstract Algebra. In particular, our focus will be on Galois Fields (also known as Finite Fields) and their applications in Computer Science. This is a project I've been excited about for many years now, but have been too busy to dedicate the adequate effort to meet my perfectionism standards (yay perfectionism!).
Backstory
Many moons back I was self-learning Galois Fields for some erasure coding theory applications. I was quite disappointed with the lack of accessible resources for computer scientists.
Many resources assumed either:
Its beyond your skill level so let's oversimplify (
"it's hard, don't worry about it"
), or
You had prior Pure Math studies in Abstract Algebra (
"it's easy, just use jargon jargon jargon"
)
Unfortunately, Abstract Algebra is not standard subject matter in most computer science curriculums. Often computer science mathematics start and end
with Discrete Math. If you're lucky, maybe you've also been exposed to Linear Algebra.
So, ultimately, I ended up self-learning Abstract Algebra from a pure math textbook. But for the great majority of computer scientists, there has to be a better way.
This series intends to fill this gap. This is the gentle step-by-step approach with applications implemented with actual code. It's the intro I wanted when I was starting out.
What is this subject?
Abstract algebra is a beautiful subject. It's the idea that the numbers you're familiar with don't matter. The numbers are just
arbitrary labels. What matters is the relationships they have with other numbers when you add or multiply them. If the numbers
don't matter, then we can swap those labels for different labels and all the normal math rules will still work.
For example, we could create an algebra that allows us to add or multiply colors:
And this is what makes the subject abstract and confusing. How can you just say that numbers don't matter? It doesn't make sense.
And even so, why would we want to study this? Why would a computer scientist care?
Well, we use computer algorithms to manipulate data. We encode/decode it, we encrypt/decrypt it, we detect corruption, etc.
Wouldn't it be great if we could use normal math to do those things? Wouldn't it be great if would could add or multiply
an 8-bit byte by an 8-bit byte and get another 8-bit byte? And if we could do that, could we also do Linear Algebra over Data? Yes, yes, and more yes.
This is why studying Abstract Algebra is worthwhile.
(Hint: Neither 263 nor 9282 are answers, they are not 8-bit numbers)
You can also make quirky blog posts that make your friends think you've gone crazy, like
milk and cookies
🥛 🍪 😊
Applications
The applications and algorithms are staggering. You interact with implementations of abstract algebra everyday: CRC,
AES Encryption, Elliptic-Curve Cryptography, Reed-Solomon, Advanced Erasure Codes, Data Hashing/Fingerprinting, Zero-Knowledge Proofs, etc.
Having a solid-background in Galois Fields and Abstract Algebra is a prerequisite for understanding these applications.
Approach: Step-by-step, Active Learning, and Literate Programming
In this series, we will start from the very basics of theory and build up step-by-step to interesting applications such as Reed-Solomon,
AES, etc. As such, the material will be
very
cumulative. Many exercises will be included to aid understanding. Each section will build gradually,
but will assume mastery of the previous section. Active learning is
strongly encouraged
. We will expect that
readers are putting in adequate effort to grok the abstract concepts.
We won't assume too much mathematical background beyond high-school level algebra. However, in some applications (for example: Reed-Solomon),
familiarity with Linear Algebra will be required. We won't explain Linear Algebra since great resources already
exist
here
. You are encouraged to supplement as needed.
We will be including code in a Literate Programming style where appropriate.  For example, to aid understanding, we will build some interactive
command-line tools that allow you to play around with various theoretical concepts in practice. All code will be the
Rust Programming Language
, but advanced features will be intentionally avoided so that the code will be readable
by most experienced computer programmers.
The main goal of this series is understandability and education. As such, the implementations will not be optimal. We will forgo nearly all
optimizations you'd see in a production quality implementation: lookup-tables, vectorized instructions, clever representations, computer
architecture optimizations, etc. It's possible that later posts in the series will discuss optimizations, but this is not a primary goal. At the end,
we hope these implementations will serve as good reference implementations. This can have it's own merit since highly optimized al

data.author: valyala
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者的内部观测平台如何从19 PiB增长到超过100 PB，处理近500万亿行数据，并成功应对了20倍事件量增长，同时CPU使用率减少到原来的10%以下。尽管OpenTelemetry（OTel）在初期有效，但随着数据规模和复杂性的增加，OTel成为瓶颈。为此，作者开发了自定义管道（SysEx），以更好地满足高性能需求，并引入了基于ClickHouse的HyperDX，提供更高效的观测体验。最终，作者转向ClickStack，这是一个围绕ClickHouse构建的端到端观测堆栈，旨在提升数据探索和根因分析的效率。文章总结了在大规模数据场景下，OTel的局限性和自定义解决方案的必要性。

44336015.article_content:
Back
Blog

Engineering
Scaling our Observability platform beyond 100 Petabytes by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
Rory Crispin
Jun 19, 2025
-
32
minutes read
TLDR
#
Observability at scale:
Our internal system grew from 19 PiB to 100 PB of uncompressed logs and from ~40 trillion to 500 trillion rows.
Efficiency breakthrough:
We absorbed a 20× surge in event volume using under 10% of the CPU previously needed.
OTel pitfalls:
The required parsing and marshalling of events in OpenTelemetry proved a bottleneck and didn’t scale - our custom pipeline addressed this.
Introducing HyperDX:
ClickHouse-native observability UI for seamless exploration, correlation, and root-cause analysis with Lucene-like syntax.
Introduction
#
About a year ago, we
shared the story of LogHouse
- our internal logging platform built to monitor ClickHouse Cloud. At the time, it managed what felt like a massive 19 PiB of data. More than just solving our observability challenges, LogHouse also saved us millions by replacing an increasingly unsustainable Datadog bill. The response to that post was overwhelming. It was clear our experience resonated with others facing similar struggles with traditional observability vendors and underscored just how critical effective data management is at scale.
A year later, LogHouse has grown beyond anything we anticipated and is now storing over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data across nearly 500 trillion rows. That kind of scale forced a series of architectural changes, new tools, and hard-earned lessons that we felt were worth sharing - not least that OpenTelemetry (OTel) isn’t always the panacea of Observability (though we still love it), and that sometimes custom pipelines are essential.
In our case, this shift enabled us to handle a 20x increase in event volume using less than 10% of the CPU for our most critical data source - a transformation with massive implications for cost and efficiency.
Other parts of our stack have also changed, not least due to the
ClickHouse acquisition of HyperDX
. Not only did this give us a first-party ClickHouse-native UI, but it also led to the
creation of ClickStack
- an opinionated, end-to-end observability stack built around ClickHouse. With HyperDX, we’ve started transitioning away from our Grafana-based custom UI, moving toward a more integrated experience for exploration, correlation, and root cause analysis.
As more teams adopt ClickHouse for observability and realize just how much they can store and query affordably, we hope these insights prove as useful as our first post. If you’re curious about this journey, when and where OTel is appropriate, and how we scaled a log pipeline to 100PB…read on.
Get started today
Interested in seeing how ClickHouse works on your data? Get started with ClickHouse Cloud in minutes and receive $300 in free credits.
Sign up
Beyond general purpose: evolving observability at scale
#
Over the past year, our approach to observability has undergone a significant transformation. We've continued to leverage OpenTelemetry to gather general-purpose logs, but as our systems have scaled, we began to reach its limits. While OTel remains a valuable part of our toolkit, it couldn't fully deliver the performance and precision we needed for our most demanding workloads. This prompted us to develop purpose-built tools tailored to our critical systems and rethink where generic solutions truly fit. Along the way, we've broadened the range of data we collect and revamped how we present insights to engineers.
A new frontier of scale
#
When we last wrote about LogHouse, we were proud to handle 19 PiB of uncompressed data across 37 trillion rows. Today, those numbers feel like a distant memory. LogHouse now stores over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data, representing nearly 500 trillion rows.
Here's a quick look at the breakdown:
System
Uncompressed Size
Stored rows
SysEx
93.6 PB
431 Trillion
OTel
14.5 PB
16.7 Trillion
These numbers also tell a story. In our original post, 100% of our telemetry flowed through OpenTelemetry, with every log line collected via the same general-purpose pipeline. But as the scale and complexity of our data grew, so did the need for specialization.
While our total volume has grown more than 5x, the breakdown reveals a deliberate shift in strategy: today, the vast majority of our data comes from “SysEx”, a new purpose-built exporter we developed to handle high-throughput, high-fidelity system logs from ClickHouse itself. This shift marks a turning point in how we think about observability pipelines - and brings us to our first key topic.
We hope the following helps comprehend the scale at which LogHouse operates.
OpenTelemetry's efficiency challenges at extreme scale
#
Initially, we used OpenTelemetry (OTel) for all log collection. It was a great starting point and an established industry standard which allowed us to quickly establish a baseline where every pod in our Kubernetes environment shipped logs to ClickHouse.

data.title: Compact Representations for Arrays in Lua [pdf]
data.author: tkhattra
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua语言中数组和表的设计以及性能优化问题

不同观点：
• [nzzn] 认为Lua使用表（table）类型来同时表示字典和数组，虽然保持了语言的简洁性，但数组在实际应用中非常常见，其他同类动态语言普遍支持数组类型。他认为数组应该成为Lua的核心语言特性，尽管对新手来说可能增加一些学习成本，但长远来看是值得的。

• [ufo] 提到数组优化的可能方案，特别是"Reflected Arrays"版本，并暗示这一优化可能会出现在Lua的下一个版本中，提供了相关链接以供参考。

• [marhee] 质疑Lua程序中是否真的经常使用具有相同类型的大型连续数组，并建议可以通过标记和单类型标签来优化这种情况，认为这样可以简单有效地优化内存使用，满足98%的使用场景。

• [Jyaif] 强烈批评Lua当前数组设计中的内存浪费问题，指出可以通过使用`__attribute__((packed))`来解决问题，并指责Lua没有在配置文件`luaconf.h`中宣传这一选项是不负责任的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Lua数组设计的简洁性与性能优化之间的平衡。一部分人认为Lua应保持简单，而另一部分人则认为应针对特定场景（如大型同类型数组）进行优化以提升性能。
• 讨论还涉及到具体的优化方案，如通过特定语法或编译选项（如`__attribute__((packed))`）来减少内存浪费。
• 时间点的提及（[kzrdude]）指出相关讨论是基于2024年9月的一个较新的发布版本，表明这是一个相对较新的问题。

data.title: Requiem for a Solar Plant
data.author: akkartik
data.article_summary: 《太阳能电厂挽歌》一文讲述了作者投资建设太阳能电厂项目从希望到破灭的过程。最初，作者希望通过将加密货币利润转化为可再生能源基础设施，以实现可持续回报和税收优惠。项目原计划容量为4.54MW，预计总成本约870万美元，但因互联研究报告显示容量需削减至3MW，且需支付近80万美元的线路升级费用，导致项目经济效益崩溃。尽管前期做了详尽分析，但因德州矿权问题、变电站距离过远及“噪音使用”等意外因素，项目无法继续。最终，作者无奈决定关闭项目，承受巨大经济损失。

44341281.article_content:
Requiem for a Solar Plant
The email landed like a brick through a plate glass window.
"...requiring reconductoring of 1.71 miles at a cost of $795,150...limiting output to 3MW..."
I stared at my laptop screen, the blue light illuminating the shadows under my eyes in my darkened California living room. Outside, endless February rain tapped against the windows like impatient fingers. My gut churned, a familiar discomfort that had become my constant companion over the past year. This wasn't just bad news. This was a death sentence.
Three years of work. Over a million dollars spent. A team scattered across three continents. All of it now threatened by two pages of engineering assessments and a single number: 3MW. My solar plant, originally planned for 4.54MW, had just been slashed by a third. The economics that had barely made sense before now collapsed entirely.
I reached for my phone and typed out a message to Mr. R.
Just saw the interconnection report. We need to talk.
The reply came quickly, despite the eleven-hour time difference. Mr. R had an uncanny ability to be available whenever needed, as though he never slept.
I've been reviewing the numbers. It doesn't work.
I rubbed my temples, remembering the day years earlier when the Invictus Solar project had first crystallized in my mind—a perfect convergence of opportunity and purpose. I'd made a fortune by accident in cryptocurrency, more money than I'd ever dreamed of, and had been searching for something meaningful to do with it. Something that would generate sustainable returns while helping shift the world toward renewable energy.
The tax advantages alone had seemed almost too good to be true: stack the federal Investment Tax Credit for solar with the capital gains deferrals from the Qualified Opportunity Zone program, and you could turn marginal economics into attractive returns. It was financial alchemy—transforming crypto profits into clean energy infrastructure while minimizing tax exposure.
Financial Projections (Pre-Interconnection Study)
- Total Installed Cost: $8,723,136 ($1.37/Watt DC)
- Capacity: 6375 kW DC / 4540 kW AC
- Net Capacity Factor: 23.8%
- Pre-tax IRR: -0.92%
- After-tax Equity IRR: 2.56%
- NPV: ($1,499,388) at 6% discount rate
- QOZ Tax Benefits: Estimated to add 3.7% to IRR
These projections relied on a $45/MWh PPA price and assumed 4.54MW AC capacity.
The reduction to 3MW in the interconnection study would significantly worsen these already-marginal returns.
Now, eighteen months later, sitting in my living room staring at the brutal economics of my failed project, I wondered how something so promising had gone so terribly wrong.
My phone rang. Mr. R.
"The land was good. The solar analysis was good. The land was flat. The price was right. The goddamn opportunity zone lined up perfectly," Mr. R said, his Russian accent more pronounced than usual, betraying his frustration. "But Texas with it's insane mineral rights and the interconnection study…"
I smiled despite myself. There was something comforting about Mr. R's exasperation, as though his anger could somehow shield us both from the disappointment.
"Tell me again what they're saying," I said, reaching for a notepad. "The whole thing."
"They want to limit us to three megawatts instead of four point five. They want us to pay nearly eight hundred thousand just to upgrade their wires. Another hundred and forty thousand for two reclosers. Plus tax." Mr. R spoke with the precision of someone who had memorized every painful detail. "And even with all that, they still say there will be fault current violations. So they cut our capacity anyway."
"Because the substation is too far away."
"Four point six miles instead of the one or two we thought. The distribution circuit takes a winding path we couldn't see from the satellite images. It goes to an entirely different substation. It's not just the distance though, our neighbors on the line have 'noisy usage' "
I stared at the ceiling, my mind racing through alternatives. Could we negotiate with the power company? Find another interconnection point? Redesign the system to work with the reduced capacity?
But I already knew the answers. We had spent months on these problems already. There was no alternative interconnection point on the property. The reduced capacity made the economics impossible. The numbers simply didn't work anymore.
"So that's it then," I said softly. "We shut it down."
The line went quiet for a moment.
"Yes," Mr. R finally said. "We shut it down. But first, I calculate exactly how much money we have wasted."
The Assembling
It started with a whiteboard session in my Palo Alto home in the summer of 2022, my kid running about in his underwear as I scribbled numbers and scenarios. Cryptocurrency had been an unexpected windfall for me, but I was painfully aware of the ecological footprint of mining. Moreover I squirmed at the 32.3% capital gains tax.

data.author: ant6n
data.article_summary: Luna Rail正在开发新一代昼夜火车，旨在优化空间利用、提升舒适度并兼顾经济性，提供比航空更环保的出行选择。其核心技术包括“酒店舱”和“座位舱”，前者为单人私密舱，白天可作起居室或移动办公室，夜间转换为舒适大床；后者为白天大座椅，夜间可平躺。通过物理模型和用户测试不断优化设计，测试显示多数用户认为这两种舱体比高铁二等座甚至一等座更具吸引力。技术目标是最大化车厢容量，使夜火车更具竞争力，并推动票价降低和线路扩展。Luna Rail还提供统一设计的应用程序，管理预订、信息和舱内控制等全程服务。

data.title: Axolotls May Hold the Key to Regrowing Limbs
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: Axolotls, a type of salamander capable of regrowing missing body parts, are helping scientists uncover the secrets of limb regeneration. In a study published in *Nature Communications*, researchers led by James Monaghan from Northeastern University genetically engineered axolotls to glow and tracked the molecular pathways involved in regeneration. They discovered that retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative, plays a crucial role in determining which type of limb should regrow, with higher concentrations leading to more extensive regrowth. The enzyme CYP26B1 controls retinoic acid levels, while the *Shox* gene is essential for proper limb regeneration. Axolotls share these genetic pathways with humans, suggesting potential for future applications in human medicine, such as developing treatments to regenerate limbs rather than form scar tissue. Though human limb regeneration is still far off, foundational research like this is crucial for progress.

主要讨论点：再生医学和肢体再生技术的科学发展及其潜在影响

不同观点：

44323562.article_content:
Axolotls are helping scientists understand the key to limb regeneration.
Alyssa Stone / Northeastern University
Axolotls have a superpower: The adorable, perpetually smiling salamanders have the ability to
regrow missing body parts
in just a few weeks. Now, in a new study that scientists say could one day help humans regenerate limbs, researchers have revealed how the animals pull this off.
“This species is special,” says lead author
James Monaghan
, a biologist at Northeastern University, to Dino Grandoni at the
Washington Post
. The amphibians have “really become the champion of some extreme abilities that animals have.”
Monaghan and his team genetically engineered
axolotls
to glow in the dark to identify the molecular pathways that allow the animals to regrow their limbs. That helped them pinpoint a molecule called retinoic acid—a derivative of vitamin A found in many skincare products—as a key ingredient for limb regeneration and examine its role. Their findings were published in the journal
Nature Communicatio
ns
on Tuesday.
Importantly, the work found that retinoic acid helps tell the axolotl which type of limb to regrow. It makes sure the animal doesn’t generate an entire arm when it only needs a hand, for example.
“This is really a question that has been fascinating developmental and regenerative biologists forever: How does the regenerating tissue know and make the blueprint of exactly what’s missing?” says
Catherine McCusker
, a developmental biologist at the University of Massachusetts Boston who was not involved in the study, to Lauren Leffer at
Popular Science
.
Unlocking the Secrets to Human Limb Regeneration
Watch on
To answer this question, the researchers, a little gruesomely, cut off the arms of axolotls. “Importantly, they don’t show signs of pain or distress after limb amputation the way mammals might, and they regenerate fully within weeks,” says Monaghan to the
Washington Post
.
Monaghan and his team tested the effects of adding varying levels of retinoic acid to the amputee axolotls, which got “pretty Frankensteiny,” he says in a
statement
. When adding too much of the acid, one axolotl grew an extra full limb out of its hand.
The team realized the salamanders have a gradient of retinoic acid throughout their arms. Near the shoulder, retinoic acid levels are higher, and the amount of the molecule decreases closer to the hands. An enzyme called CYP26B1 breaks down retinoic acid and controls how much of it exists at each part of the body, the research found. So, a small level of retinoic acid will result in the salamander producing just a finger or toe, while a larger amount will generate a whole arm or leg.
The researchers also identified a gene called
Shox
as important to this process—it’s one of the genes that retinoic acid targets in the axolotl’s cells, according to the statement. When the level of retinoic acid signaling in the axolotls went up, the
Shox
gene turned on, which suggests it’s a key part of how axolotls regenerate limbs. When the scientists used a gene editing tool called CRISPR-Cas9 to remove the gene from the axolotl’s DNA, the animals grew normal-sized hands but produced very short arms.
“Evidence suggests it’s the access to the appropriate genes after an injury that enable them to regenerate an arm. So they can turn on those programs that built the arm in the first place,” Monaghan explains to Meryl Davids Landau at
National Geographic
, referring to the
Shox
gene.
Humans also have retinoic acid and the
Shox
gene, which means we share the genetic pathways that allow axolotls to regrow body parts—the challenge is how to unlock their power, experts say. Once scientists figure that out, it might lead to “restoring greater regenerative potential than we currently see,” says
Thomas Rando
, director of the Broad Stem Cell Research Center at the University of California, Los Angeles, who was not involved in the study, to
National Geographic
.
Monaghan adds to the publication that he can envision future researchers engineering a patch that would reprogram human cells to regenerate a limb rather than create scar tissue after severe injury.
Getting humans to regrow missing limbs is still a long way down the road, but more foundational research—like this new paper—can help scientists get there, McCusker tells
Popular Science
. “We need to remember to continue to invest in these basic biology studies,” she adds.

They discovered that retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative, plays a crucial role in determining which type of limb should regrow, with higher concentrations leading to more extensive regrowth. data.title: Sound As Pure Form: Music Language Inspired by Supercollider, APL, and Forth
data.author: mindcrime
data.article_summary: "Sound As Pure Form" (sapf) 是一个用于音频合成的解释器，采用类似Forth的语法，支持懒惰列表和类似APL的自动映射。该语言功能性强、基于栈、使用后缀表示法，旨在通过高层次的函数和自动映射、扫描、归约操作符处理音频和控制事件。sapf受APL、Joy、Haskell等语言启发，强调简洁表达和并发处理能力。其特点包括函数组合自然、无需考虑操作优先级和分隔符、支持多返回值等。虽然受启于连接式编程，但sapf包含词法变量。设置包括将程序放入执行路径、去除苹果的隔离属性、配置环境变量，并可通过命令行运行和查看示例。

• **lfnoise（SAPF 作者）**：简要介绍了 SAPF 的历史，指出其在2011年编写并最近才开源。同时提及自己在音频合成实验和 SuperCollider 方面的贡献。

WHAT
This program is called:
"A tool for exploring sound as pure form." or "sound as pure form" or "sapf"
It is an interpreter for a language for creating and transforming sound. The
language is mostly functional, stack based and uses postfix notation similar to
FORTH. It represents audio and control events using lazy, possibly infinite
sequences. It intends to do for lazy sequences what APL does for arrays: provide
very high level functions with pervasive automatic mapping, scanning, and
reduction operators. This makes for a language where short programs can achieve
results out of proportion to their size. Because nearly all of the programmer
accessible data types are immutable, the language can easily run multiple
threads without deadlock or corruption.
WHY
Other languages that inspired this one:
APL, Joy[1], Haskell, Piccola[2], Nyquist[3], SuperCollider[4].
APL and FORTH (from which Joy derives) are both widely derided for being
write-only languages. Nevertheless, there has yet to be a language of such
concise expressive power as APL or its descendants. APL is powerful not because
of its bizarre symbols or syntax, but due to the way it automatically maps
operations over arrays and allows iterations at depth within arrays. This means
one almost never needs to write a loop or think about operations one-at-a-time.
Instead one can think about operations on whole structures.
Here is a great quote from Alan Perlis[5] on APL, which that also reflects my
interest in this way of programming :
"What attracted me, then, to APL was a feeling that perhaps through APL one
might begin to acquire some of the dimensions in programming that we revere in
natural language — some of the pleasures of composition; of saying things
elegantly; of being brief, poetic, artistic, that makes our natural languages
so precious to us."
The Joy language introduced concatenative functional programming. This generally
means a stack based virtual machine, and a program consisting of words which are
functions taking an input stack and returning an output stack. The natural
syntax that results is postfix. Over a very long time I have come to feel that
syntax gets in between me and the power in a language. Postfix is the least
syntax possible.
There are several reasons I like the concatenative style of programming:
Function composition is concatenation.
Pipelining values through functions to get new values is the most natural
idiom.
Functions are applied from left to right instead of inside out.
Support for multiple return values comes for free.
No need for operator precedence.
Fewer delimiters are required:
Parentheses are not needed to control operator precedence.
Semicolons are not needed to separate statements.
Commas are not needed to separate arguments.
(Note: Sapf is inspired by, but is not purely a concatenative language because it has lexical variables.)
When I am programming interactively, I most often find myself in the situation
where I have a value and I want to transform it to something else. The thing to
do is apply a function with some parameters. With concatenative programming this
is very natural. You string along several words and get a new value.
QUICK SET-UP
Put the sapf program into ~/bin or wherever you keep commands.
Since this binary is unsigned you will need to remove Apple's quarantine attribute:
xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine <path-to-sapf-binary>
Set up the environment variables in Terminal or your shell profile.
For example:
export SAPF_HISTORY="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-history.txt"
export SAPF_LOG="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-log.txt"
export SAPF_PRELUDE="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-prelude.txt"
export SAPF_EXAMPLES="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-examples.txt"
export SAPF_README="$HOME/sapf-files/README.txt"
export SAPF_RECORDINGS="$HOME/sapf-files/recordings"
export SAPF_SPECTROGRAMS="$HOME/sapf-files/spectrograms"
read this README.
check out some examples:
start sapf in Terminal.
open sapf-examples.txt in a text editor
copy an example onto the command line.
COMMAND LINE
sapf [-r sample-rate][-p prelude-file]
sapf [-h]
print this help
OPTIONS
-r sample-rate
Sets the session sample rat

data.title: TPU Deep Dive
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了谷歌TPU（Tensor Processing Units）的设计理念和内部结构，强调其可扩展性、高吞吐量和能效。TPU是谷歌为满足人工智能计算需求而开发的专用集成电路（ASIC），特别擅长处理大规模矩阵乘法和神经网络计算。TPU的强大性能得益于硬件（如能量效率和模块化设计）和软件（如XLA编译器）的协同设计。

TPU的单芯片包含两个TensorCore，每个TensorCore具有共享内存和专门的计算单元，如矩阵乘法单元（MXU）、向量单元（VPU）等。TPU采用脉动阵列设计，通过流水线技术实现高吞吐量，特别适合矩阵乘法和卷积操作。然而，脉动阵列对稀疏矩阵的处理效率较低。

相较于GPU，TPU拥有更大的片上内存和更少的计算核心，但通过优化设计实现了极高的计算效率。例如，TPUv5p单芯片可达500 TFLOPs/秒，而TPUv7整个计算单元可达42.5 ExaFLOPs/秒。

总体而言，TPU通过独特的设计选择，在处理AI任务上展现了出色的性能和能效。

44342977.article_content:
I've been working with TPUs a lot recently and it's fun to see how they had such different design philosophies compared to GPUs.
The main strongpoint for TPUs is in their scalability. This is achieved through a co-design of both the hardware side (e.g. energy efficiency and modularity) and the software side (e.g. XLA compiler).
Background
To give a brief tldr on TPUs, it's
Google's ASIC that focuses on two factors: extreme matmul throughput + energy efficiency.
Their origins go back to Google in 2006, when they were first evaluating whether they should implement either GPUs, FPGAs, or custom ASICs. Back then there were only a few applications that necessitated specialized hardware and they decided those needs could be met by bringing in excess CPU compute from their large datacenters. But this changed in 2013 when Google's voice search feature ran on neural networks and internal projections speculated that they would need much more compute if it took off.
Fast forward to today and TPUs power the majority of Google's AI services. Of course, that includes training and inference of Gemini or Veo, but also deploying their recommendation models (DLRMs).
Let's dive in and look at TPU internals from the bottom up.
TPU Single-Chip Level
I'll focus my diagrams to TPUv4, but this layout is more or less applicable to latest generation TPUs (e.g. TPUv6p "Trillium"; TPUv7 "Ironwood's details aren't released as of writing in June, 2025).
Here's the layout of a single TPUv4 chip:
TPU Single Chip + TensorCore
In each chip, there's two TPU TensorCores, which are responsible for our compute. (Note: inference-specialized TPUs have only one TensorCore). Both TensorCores have shared memory units: CMEM(128MiB) and HBM(32GiB).
And within each TensorCore, there lies our compute units and smaller memory buffers:
1. Matrix Multiply Unit (MXU)
- This is the key component of the TensorCore and is a 128x128 systolic array.
- We'll cover systolic arrays below.
2. Vector Unit (VPU)
- General elementwise operations (e.g. ReLU, pointwise add/mul, reductions)
3. Vector Memory (VMEM; 32MiB)
- Memory buffer. Data from HBM is copied into the VMEM before the TensorCore can do any computations.
4. Scalar Unit + Scalar Memory (SMEM; 10MiB)
- Tell the VPU and MXU what to do.
- Manages control flow, scalar operations, and memory address generation.
If you're coming from NVIDIA GPUs, there's some initial observations that might throw you off:
On-chip memory units (CMEM, VMEM, SMEM) on TPUs are much larger than L1, L2 caches on GPUs.
HBM on TPUs are also much smaller than HBM on GPUs.
There seems to be a lot less "cores" responsible for the computation.
This is the complete opposite of GPUs where they have smaller L1, L2 caches (256KB and 50MB, respectively for H100), larger HBM (80GB for H100), and tens of thousands of cores.
Before we go any further, recall that TPUs are capable of extremely high throughput just like GPUs. TPU v5p can achieve 500 TFLOPs/sec per chip and with a full pod of 8960 chips we can achieve approximately 4.45 ExaFLOPs/sec. The newest "Ironwood" TPUv7 is said to reach up to 42.5 ExaFLOPS/sec per pod (9216 chips).
To understand how TPUs achieve this, we need to understand their design philosophy.
TPU Design Philosophy
TPUs achieve amazing throughput and energy efficiency by relying on two large pillars and a key assumption: systolic arrays + pipelining, Ahead-of-Time (AoT) compilation, and the assumption that most operations can be expressed in a way that maps well to systolic arrays. Fortunately, in our modern DL era, matmuls comprise the bulk of computation, which are fit for systolic arrays.
TPU Design choice #1: Systolic Arrays + Pipelining
Q. What is a Systolic Array?
Systolic array is a hardware design architecture consisting of a grid of interconnected processing elements (PE). Each PE performs a small computation (e.g. multiply and accumulate) and passes the results to neighboring PEs.
The benefit of such a design is that once data is passed into a systolic array, additional control logic on how data should be processed is not required. Also, when given a large enough systolic array, there's no memory read/writes other than the input and output.
Due to their rigid organization, systolic arrays can only handle operations with fixed dataflow patterns, but fortunately matrix multiplication and convolutions fit perfectly in this regime.
Moreover, there's clear opportunities for pipelining to overlap computation with data movements. Here's a diagram below for a pipelined pointwise operation on a TPU.
Pipelined Pointwise Operation (from "How to Scale Your Model"
[4]
)
Aside: Downsides of Systolic Arrays - Sparsity
You can see how systolic arrays love dense matrices (i.e. When every PE is active nearly every cycle). However, the downside is that there's no performance improvements for sparse matrices of the same size: the same number of cycles will have to be performed where PEs are still doing work even for zero-valued eleme
44342977.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了谷歌TPU（Tensor Processing Units）的设计理念和内部结构，强调其可扩展性、高吞吐量和能效。TPU是谷歌为满足人工智能计算需求而开发的专用集成电路（ASIC），特别擅长处理大规模矩阵乘法和神经网络计算。TPU的强大性能得益于硬件（如能量效率和模块化设计）和软件（如XLA编译器）的协同设计。

TPU的单芯片包含两个TensorCore，每个TensorCore具有共享内存和专门的计算单元，如矩阵乘法单元（MXU）、向量单元（VPU）等。TPU采用脉动阵列设计，通过流水线技术实现高吞吐量，特别适合矩阵乘法和卷积操作。然而，脉动阵列对稀疏矩阵的处理效率较低。

相较于GPU，TPU拥有更大的片上内存和更少的计算核心，但通过优化设计实现了极高的计算效率。例如，TPUv5p单芯片可达500 TFLOPs/秒，而TPUv7整个计算单元可达42.5 ExaFLOPs/秒。

总体而言，TPU通过独特的设计选择，在处理AI任务上展现了出色的性能和能效。

data.title: Remote MCP Support in Claude Code
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: Claude Code宣布支持远程MCP服务器，用户可以将第三方工具和数据源集成到编码环境中，而无需管理本地服务器。通过连接MCP服务器，Claude Code能够访问如开发工具、项目管理系统和知识库等服务，并在其中执行操作。例如，与Sentry MCP服务器集成后，可以在终端中直接调试问题；与Linear MCP服务器集成后，可以获取项目和问题详情，减少切换界面的需要。远程MCP服务器由供应商维护，用户只需添加服务器URL，Claude Code支持原生OAuth以确保连接安全。该功能现已上线，用户可查看文档或MCP目录开始使用。

Product
Remote MCP support in Claude Code
Jun 18, 2025
●
2 min
read
Today, we’re announcing support for remote MCP servers in Claude Code. Connect your favorite tools and data sources to personalize your coding experience without needing to manage local servers.
Using Claude Code as your primary development interface
Claude Code can access both tools and resources exposed by MCP servers, giving it the ability to pull context from your third-party services—such as dev tools, project management systems, and knowledge bases—and take actions within those services.
You can integrate Claude Code with any remote MCP server, and the growing ecosystem of servers means that new capabilities are constantly coming online.
For example, by integrating Claude Code with the Sentry MCP server, you can access errors and issues from Sentry. Then, you can debug using the context of those issues without leaving your terminal.
You can also integrate Claude Code with the Linear MCP server to work with the context of your active projects.
“Linear's MCP integration brings Linear projects and issues directly into Claude Code,” shares Tom Moor, Head of Engineering at Linear. “With structured, real-time context from Linear, Claude Code can pull in issue details and project status—engineers can now stay in flow when moving between planning, writing code, and managing issues. Fewer tabs, less copy-paste. Better software, faster.”
Seamless connections with minimal maintenance
Remote MCP servers offer a lower maintenance alternative to local servers: just add the vendor’s URL to Claude Code—no manual setup required. Vendors handle updates, scaling, and availability, so you can focus on building instead of managing server infrastructure.
Claude Code also features native OAuth support for remote MCP servers, ensuring secure connections to your existing accounts. Simply authenticate to your servers once, and Claude Code handles the rest—no API keys to manage or credentials to store.
Getting started
Remote MCP server support is available now in Claude Code. View the
documentation
to get started or explore our
MCP directory
with recommended servers.

data.title: Mbake – A Makefile formatter and linter, that only took 50 years
data.author: rainmans
data.article_summary: **mbake** 是一个用于格式化和检查 Makefile 的工具。它提供可配置的格式规则、CI/CD 集成、扩展插件架构、丰富的终端输出和语法验证等功能。主要功能包括规范缩进与间距、处理换行符、智能合并连续行、自动插入和增强 `.PHONY` 声明等。安装可通过 PyPI 或 VSCode 插件完成，使用简单的命令行接口进行格式化和验证操作。支持自定义配置文件，并提供多种选项用于控制格式化和验证行为，如备份文件、显示差异、验证语法等。此外，还支持版本管理和 shell 命令补全。

data.article_summary: 文章报道了世界上最大的野生动物天桥——**沃利斯·安嫩伯格野生动物通道**的最新建设进展。该项目位于加州阿古拉山，横跨101号公路，旨在帮助包括美洲狮在内的野生动物安全穿越繁忙的公路，恢复栖息地的连通性。自2022年开工以来，桥梁的主体结构已接近完成，使用了2600万磅的混凝土。下一步将铺设6000立方码的“超级土壤”，并种植5000株本地植物，以创造适合野生动物的栖息地。该天桥预计明年完工，建成后将减少野生动物因交通事故死亡的风险，并改善区域生态健康。文章还提到，著名美洲狮P-22的经历突显了这一项目的重要性。

Three years after construction began, it’s time to dump dirt on the project. Specifically, 6,000 cubic yards of a “super” soil followed by the planting of 5,000 native flora. I’m talking about the world’s
largest wildlife crossing
, which has reached another construction milestone as the bridge nears completion.
This
prepared soil
is the beginning of the end of construction for the
Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing
, which broke ground on Earth Day in 2022. Located in Agoura Hills, California, the nearly one-acre overpass stretches over a 10-lane section of U.S. 101.
The physical bridge structure is essentially complete, having required 26 million pounds of concrete, Beth Pratt of the National Wildlife Federation (NWF) told
KCAL
. The NWF Regional Executive Director added, “We just put the soil on top, and then we start burying utility lines and extend it over the access road.”
Multiple layers of soil will be needed to create a wildlife habitat on the overpass, and the soil application alone will take several weeks. However, when the Annenberg Wildlife Crossing is done, the bridge will reconnect the bisected areas of the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area. With more than 150,000 acres, SMMNRA is the country’s largest urban national park. But the freeways have long isolated the local fauna, from butterflies and cottontails to bobcats and mountain lions.
According to the
project
, as far back as the 1980s, researchers identified the Liberty Canyon area as a choke point for wildlife. However, it wasn’t until the
National Park Service
began a decades-long study of the region’s mountain lion population that the 101 freeway was deemed “the most significant barrier to the ecological health of the region.”
More than 300,000 vehicles travel along U.S. 101 daily. That’s enough traffic to give a driver anxiety—try being a
local critter
having to dart across the road just to find dinner.
P-22
, arguably the most famous mountain lion in and outside of Hollywood, surprised everyone by crossing freeways on his own. He eventually became the poster cat for the “Save L.A. cougars” campaign. Unfortunately, he was euthanized in late 2022 after being found with severe injuries, likely due to a vehicle collision, and a myriad of other health issues.
Mountain lions are the main conservation focus of this
wildlife bridge
. The big cats are territorial, and being locked in by freeways limits their roaming range and biodiversity. Without the crossing to expand their habitat, SoCal cougars could be extinct within 50 years. They also continue to be killed by vehicles.
“In the Liberty Canyon area where we’re putting the crossing, within the last four years, we’ve had four mountain lions killed just in that general area,” Pratt said.
Not just providing access to more sources of food, shelter, and mates, but the bridge would also offer an escape route from wildfires and other disasters. The Annenberg Wildlife Crossing is expected to reach completion next year.

主要讨论点： submarine电影的评价与推荐

不同观点：
• [fracus] 和 [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为《Office Space》虽然是喜剧，但准确描绘了潜艇工作中的繁文缛节和工程师的孤立状态。相比之下，[ChrisMarshallNY] 更喜欢《Das Boot》，并提到德国电影行业的表现出色。
• [rwmj] 认为观看《Das Boot》后还有人自愿参军是很勇敢的，暗示该电影真实呈现了潜艇生活的压力和恐惧。
• [johannes1234321] 推荐《Das Boot》的DVD版本，尤其是导演剪辑版，因为这些版本更好地展现了潜艇生活的单调和紧张感。
• [avoutos] 强调《Das Boot》的配乐通过合成器、机械声音和声纳ping声，增强了电影的封闭感和压迫感。
• [southernplaces7] 详细分析了《Das Boot》的制作细节，如演员的训练和场景的真实性，认为该电影是对潜艇生活的最真实描绘，并将其与太空旅行相比较。
• [nemosaltat] 认为高级军官的意见在此调查中占比过大，并提出《Down Periscope》更准确地捕捉了潜艇生活中的荒谬和无聊。
• [gcanyon] 表示虽然《Das Boot》是预料中的答案，但其他例外回答也值得关注。
• [zabzonk] 提到《Operation Petticoat》是一部有趣的潜艇喜剧电影。
• [jmcgough] 对《Down Periscope》被提及感到有趣，并表示自己首先想到的也是这部电影。
• [adt] 建议直接询问实际的潜艇船员，以获取更真实的电影评价。
• [Hilift] 推荐了《On the Beach (1959)》这部末日题材的潜艇电影。
• [anonymousiam] 认为《Das Boot》最真实，同时推荐了《Crimson Tide》和《The Hunt For Red October》作为更具戏剧性的选择。
• [DocTomoe] 提到了《The Fifth Missile (1986)》这部电影，认为其描绘潜艇成员因有毒油漆导致精神错乱的剧情值得关注。

data.title: Harry Brearley, the creator of stainless steel (2016)
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了哈里·布莱尔利（Harry Brearley）童年时期在英国谢菲尔德贫穷环境下对钢铁生产的浓厚兴趣，以及他后来成为不锈钢发明者的经历。哈里从小生活困窘，家里没有书籍和玩具，他通过在街头观察各种工匠和工厂工人学习技艺。尤其对钢铁厂的操作着迷，常常偷偷溜进去观看。他特别喜欢观看铁匠进行的金属韧性测试，并立志生产高质量的钢铁。这种早期接触奠定了他一生致力于钢铁研究的基础，最终发明了不锈钢。哈里的成长环境虽然艰苦，但他的好奇心和热情使他克服困难，成为杰出的冶金学家。

不同观点：

44346529.article_content:
S
ometime in 1882, a skinny, dark-haired, 11-year-old boy named Harry Brearley entered a steelworks for the first time. A shy kid—he was scared of the dark, and a picky eater—he was also curious, and the industrial revolution in Sheffield, England, offered much in the way of amusements. He enjoyed wandering around town—he later called himself a Sheffield Street Arab—watching road builders, bricklayers, painters, coal deliverers, butchers, and grinders. He was drawn especially to workshops; if he couldn’t see in a shop window, he would knock on the door and offer to run an errand for the privilege of watching whatever work was going on inside. Factories were even more appealing, and he had learned to gain access by delivering, or pretending to deliver, lunch or dinner to an employee. Once inside, he must have reveled, for not until the day’s end did he emerge, all grimy and gray but for his blue eyes. Inside the steelworks, the action compelled him so much that he spent hours sitting inconspicuously on great piles of coal, breathing through his mouth, watching brawny men shoveling fuel into furnaces, hammering white-hot ingots of iron.

There was one operation in particular that young Harry liked: a toughness test performed by the blacksmith. After melting and pouring a molten mixture from a crucible, the blacksmith would cast a bar or two of that alloy, and after it cooled, he would cut notches in the ends of those bars. Then he’d put the bars in a vise, and hammer away at them.
The effort required to break the metal bars, as interpreted through the blacksmith’s muscles, could vary by an order of magnitude, but the result of the test was expressed qualitatively. The metal was pronounced on the spot either rotten or darned good stuff. The latter was simply called D.G.S. The aim of the men at that steelworks, and every other, was to produce D.G.S., and Harry took that to heart.

In this way, young Harry became familiar with steelmaking long before he formally taught himself as much as there was to know about the practice. It was the beginning of a life devoted to steel, without the distractions of hobbies, vacations, or church. It was the origin of a career in which Brearley wrote eight books on metals, five of which contain the word steel in the title; in which he could argue about steelmaking—but not politics—all night; and in which the love and devotion he bestowed upon inanimate metals exceeded that which he bestowed upon his parents or wife or son. Steel was Harry’s true love. It would lead, eventually, to the discovery of stainless steel.
H
arry Brearley was born on Feb. 18, 1871, and grew up poor, in a small, cramped house on Marcus Street, in Ramsden’s Yard, on a hill in Sheffield. The city was the world capital of steelmaking; by 1850 Sheffield steelmakers produced half of all the steel in Europe, and 90 percent of the steel in England. By 1860, no fewer than 178 edge tool and saw makers were registered in Sheffield. In the first half of the 19th century, as Sheffield rose to prominence, the population of the city grew fivefold, and its filth grew proportionally. A saying at the time, that “where there’s muck there’s money,” legitimized the grime, reek, and dust of industrial Sheffield, but Harry recognized later that it was a misfortune to be from there, for nobody had much ambition.
The house Harry grew up in was sparse and tight; the living room measured 10 feet square, with two bedrooms above it. The kids ate standing up because there were not enough chairs. There were no books, or pictures, or toys; there was no space for a desk. The Brearleys were heartily poor but not starving, yet they weren’t far from the breadline. Harry wore jackets that had been made from his father’s trousers. He helped deliver coal in a wheelbarrow in return for sweets. After school, he bundled sticks, earning a penny for a dozen bundles. He used to walk along nearby railroad tracks, collect lumps of coal that had fallen from passing trains, and bring them home to his mother. He once borrowed a book from the library, and copied it—the whole thing—by hand, because he couldn’t afford to buy a copy. In 1882 his parents moved down to Carlisle Street, beside the railroad tracks—a place said to be separated from hell by only a sheet of tissue paper. It was filthier, dustier, smokier. But Harry loved it, on account of the increased color and variety. There was a pigsty and stables to poke around in, and more adult conversation to pick up. On account of his curiosity, he was regularly late for school; he found too much to look at on the way. He got away from school, at age 11, with his “brains unshackled and his curiosity undimmed,” and was then free to work, according to the law, in nonfactory conditions.

data.title: Load Test GlassFlow for ClickHouse: Real-Time Dedup at Scale
data.author: super_ar
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了对GlassFlow在ClickHouse实时去重管道中的负载测试结果。GlassFlow是一个开源的流式ETL服务，专为ClickHouse设计，用于处理Kafka流数据。测试在一个MacBook Pro上进行，模拟了每秒55,000条记录的负载，GlassFlow以每秒处理9,000+条记录的速度运行，延迟低于0.12毫秒。测试显示，即使在处理2,000万条记录和12个并发发布者时，系统依然稳定，无崩溃、无数据丢失和乱序。

测试使用了模拟用户事件数据的合成数据，基础设施包括Docker中的Kafka、ClickHouse和GlassFlow。测试逐步增加数据量，从500万条记录到2,000万条，并调整多个参数以观察性能变化。结果表明，GlassFlow在高负载下仍能保持高效和可靠的去重能力。

测试代码和设置文档已开源，供用户自行尝试：
- 代码库: https://github.com/glassflow/clickhouse-etl-loadtest
- 文档: https://docs.glassflow.dev/load-test/setup

GlassFlow支持实时去重、流式连接、恰好一次语义和原生ClickHouse写入，旨在解决从Kafka到ClickHouse实时数据管道中的去重和延迟问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GlassFlow的高吞吐性能表现及其测试结果，以及是否必须为可扩展性和可靠性牺牲效率。

不同观点：
• Ashish和Armend（GlassFlow创始人）分享了GlassFlow的负载测试结果，展示了其在处理高吞吐数据流（如Kafka到ClickHouse）时的性能表现。他们强调其工具在2000万条记录的测试中，实现了每秒9000条以上的去重记录处理能力，且端到端延迟低于0.12毫秒。他们还提供了详细的博客文章和文档，以便其他人可以复现测试。

• kI3RO指出了一个技术问题：他们的网站没有滚动条，导致无法阅读内容。这是一个关于用户体验的技术问题，可能影响其他人获取详细信息。

• api则对性能表现提出了不同的看法，认为在本地设备（如Raspberry Pi 5）上运行高效代码也能达到类似性能，不需要特别高的硬件配置。他还质疑了在实现可扩展性、冗余性和自动重部署等功能时，是否必须牺牲如此多的效率，认为当前的技术栈可能会带来数量级的性能损失。

补充讨论：
• 关于GlassFlow性能的讨论主要集中在高吞吐处理能力和低延迟上，创始人提供了详细的测试结果和复现方法，希望获得社区的反馈，特别是来自高吞吐ClickHouse用户的反馈。

• api的观点引出了一个更广泛的讨论：在追求分布式系统的高可用性和可扩展性时，是否不可避免地要牺牲单机效率。这个问题涉及到系统架构设计中的权衡，可能需要考虑具体的应用场景和技术需求。

• kI3RO提出的网站问题虽然是个小问题，但指出了技术产品在用户体验上的细节，可能影响用户获取信息和使用体验。

ClickHouse
Load Test GlassFlow for ClickHouse: Real-Time Deduplication at Scale
Benchmarking GlassFlow: Fast, reliable deduplication at 20M events
Written by
Ashish Bagri
06/06/2025, 08.07
Load Test GlassFlow for ClickHouse: Real-Time Deduplication at Scale
By Ashish Bagri, Co-founder & CTO of GlassFlow
TL;DR
We tested GlassFlow on a real-world deduplication pipeline with Kafka and ClickHouse.
It handled 55,00 records/sec published by Kafka and processed 9,000+ records/sec on a MacBook Pro, with sub-0.12ms latency.
No crashes, no message loss, no disordering. Even with 20M records and 12 concurrent publishers, it remained robust.
Want to try it yourself? The full test setup is open source:
https://github.com/glassflow/clickhouse-etl-loadtest
and the docs
https://docs.glassflow.dev/load-test/setup
Why this test?
ClickHouse is incredible at fast analytics. But when building real-time pipelines from Kafka to ClickHouse, many teams run into the same issues: analytics results are incorrect or too delayed to support real-time use cases.
The root cause? Data duplications and slow joins. They are often introduced by retries, offset reprocessing, or downstream enrichment. These problems can affect both correctness and performance.
That’s why we built GlassFlow: A real-time streaming ETL engine designed to process Kafka streams
before
data hits ClickHouse.
After launching the product, we often received the question, “
How does it perform at high loads?
”
With this post, we want to give a clear and reproducible answer to that. This article walks through what we tested, how we set it up, and what we found when testing deduplications with GlassFlow.
What is GlassFlow?
GlassFlow is an open-source streaming ETL service developed specifically for ClickHouse. It is a real-time stream processing solution designed to simplify data pipeline creation and management between Kafka and ClickHouse. It supports:
Real-time deduplication
(configurable window, event ID based)
Stream joins
between topics
Exactly-once semantics
Native ClickHouse sink
with efficient batching and buffering
GlassFlow handles the hard parts: state, ordering, retries and batching.
More about GlassFlow at our prev HN post
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43953722
Test Assumptions
Before we dive in, here’s what you should know about how we ran the test.
Data Used:
Simulating a Real-World Use Case
For this benchmark, we use synthetic data that simulates a real-world use case: logging user events in an application.
Each record represents an event triggered by a user, similar to what you'd see in analytics or activity tracking systems.
Here's the schema:
Field
Type
Description
event_id
UUID (v4)
Unique ID for the event
user_id
UUID (v4)
Unique ID for the user
name
String
Full name of the user
email
String
User’s email address
created_at
Datetime (
%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S
)
Timestamp of when the event occurred
This structure helps simulate insert-heavy workloads and time-based queries—perfect for testing how GlassFlow performs with ClickHouse in a realistic, high-volume setting.
Infrastructure Setup
For this benchmark, we will be running the load test locally using Docker to simulate the entire data pipeline. The setup included:
Kafka
: Running in a Docker container to handle event streaming.
ClickHouse
: Also containerized, serving as the storage layer.
GlassFlow ETL
: Deployed in Docker, responsible for processing messages from Kafka and writing them to ClickHouse.
While the setup supports running against cloud-hosted Kafka and ClickHouse, we chose to keep everything local to maintain control over the environment and ensure consistent test conditions.
Each test run automatically creates the necessary Kafka topics and ClickHouse tables before starting, and cleans them up afterward. This keeps the environment clean between runs and ensures reproducible results.
Resource Used for Testing
The load tests were conducted on a MacBook Pro with the following specifications:
Specification
Details
Model Name
MacBook Pro
Model Identifier
Mac14,5
Model Number
MPHG3D/A
Chip
Apple M2 Max
Total Number of Cores
12 (8 performance and 4 efficiency)
Memory
32 GB
Additional Assumptions
Furthermore, to push our implementation to the limits, we do the following:
We use an example where we have incoming data with some amount of duplication (10%, to be exact) and we need to deduplicate it.
We perform incremental tests with growing data volume at each step (starting from 5 million records moving our way up to 20 million records).
Apart from this, we also change several parameters and see how that impacts our overall performance.
So, let’s start with the actual test.
Running the Actual Load Test
We created a load test repo so you can run this benchmark yourself in minutes (
check it out here
). Using this, we ran a series of local load tests that mimicked a real-time streaming setup. The goal was simple: push a steady stream of user event data through a Kafka → GlassFlow → ClickHouse pipelin

data.article_summary: Lungy是一款由医生开发的呼吸应用，通过识别和回应用户的呼吸来帮助他们感到更平静和放松。该应用已在40多个国家推广，拥有超过10万名用户，被誉为“最美的呼吸应用”。它提供独特的呼吸练习，无需网络连接，并支持个性化进度和反馈。免费版提供日常呼吸练习，而付费版Lungy Deluxe则提供全部练习、自定义和详细报告。最新版本集成了HealthKit，支持Apple Watch的健康指标。用户评价积极，认为其设计简洁美观，对睡眠和放松有帮助。隐私和数据安全也得到了保障。

data.title: Using an $8 smart outlet to avoid brainrot
data.author: NWChen
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种利用8美元智能插座防止分心的方法。作者编写了一个后台运行的脚本，监控智能插座的状态。该插座可通过WiFi连接，并提供API查询开关状态。当插座开关打开时，脚本会修改**/etc/hosts**文件，屏蔽特定网站（如Twitter、YouTube等）。插座可以插在远离用户的电源插座上，用户若想访问被屏蔽的网站，必须起身手动关闭插座开关。这一额外步骤增加了操作难度，有效减少了无意识的分心行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过技术手段控制上网行为和减少分心

不同观点：
• 使用智能插座定时关闭Wi-Fi：有用户通过设置智能插座定时关闭Wi-Fi，并结合电脑提醒，给自己15分钟的收尾时间，以此减少上网时间。
• 使用One Sec应用程序：有用户推荐One Sec应用，通过在访问特定网站前强制进行呼吸练习来减少冲动访问，认为该应用对某些人有显著效果，但也指出并非所有解决方案都适用于每个人。
• 结合运动与上网时间：有用户建议将智能插座与运动设备结合，比如在使用步行垫时才允许访问特定网站，或者开发一个小应用程序来跟踪运动时间并限制上网时间。
• 改进开关设计：有用户认为使用按键代替开关会更有效，避免用户长时间保持Wi-Fi开启状态，建议使用Amazon Dash按钮进行这种改进。
• 使用uBlock Origin和自定义过滤列表：有用户通过uBlock Origin的自定义过滤列表来阻止访问特定网站，认为这是一种有效的解决方案，但对于更严重的成瘾问题可能需要投资购买付费工具。
• 使用Foqos应用程序和NFC标签：有用户分享使用Foqos应用程序和NFC标签的组合，通过配置NFC标签来限制手机应用程序的使用，认为这是一种有效的解决方案。

data.title: How fast are Linux pipes anyway?
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Linux中Unix管道的实现和性能优化。作者通过一个简单的测试程序逐步优化管道读写速度，从最初的3.5GiB/s提升到约36GiB/s。优化过程包括使用`perf`工具进行性能分析，介绍`vmsplice`和`splice`系统调用以提升性能，以及通过使用大页面（huge pages）进一步改进。最终，通过将轮询改为忙等待（busy looping）完成最后的优化。文章详细解释了每一步的原理，包括管道的内部实现、Linux分页机制等，并提供了代码示例和性能对比图。测试在Intel Skylake i7-8550U CPU和Linux 5.17上进行，结果会因系统环境不同而有所变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux与Windows在管道（pipes）操作上的性能差异及技术实现细节，以及对具体技术如splice()的讨论和其未来发展的疑问。

不同观点：
• [zh3] 分享了将基于Linux管道的应用程序移植到Windows上的糟糕性能体验，指出Windows在处理管道连接时的性能问题，甚至在使用C#和Win10时性能差距依然显著。
• [johnisgood] 讨论了Linux和BSD系统中不同的高效数据传输方式，特别提到splice()在Linux上的零拷贝优势，以及在BSD系统上readv() / writev()可能是更有效的方法。
• [gkfasdfasdf] 仅仅提到文章之前在其他平台被讨论过，没有提出新的技术观点。
• [lukeh] 询问现代Linux是否有类似于Solaris Doors的机制，用于低延迟的小数据量进程间通信，认为AF_UNIX可能不是最佳选择。
• [gigatexal] 对文章本身表示赞赏，未提出技术性讨论。
• [aeonik] 对文章缺乏评论表示遗憾，同时对splice()的安全性和ABI破坏问题表示关注，并好奇splice()的长期支持以及是否能默认使用splice()来优化管道性能。

补充讨论：
• [johnisgood] 提到了多种数据传输函数如readv() / writev()、splice()、sendfile()等，并详细分析了splice()在Linux上的高效性，但也指出了其仅限于Linux系统的局限性。
• [lukeh] 提出了对Linux系统中进程间通信的低延迟替代方案的需求，特别是与AF_UNIX的对比。
• [aeonik] 对splice()的长期支持表示不确定，并提出是否有可能通过默认使用splice()来提升管道性能的设想。

争议焦点：
• Linux和Windows在管道操作上的性能差异，尤其是Windows在处理等待连接的管道时的表现较差。
• 关于splice()在Linux上的使用及其未来发展的不确定性，特别是其安全性及ABI破坏问题。
• 对Linux系统中低延迟进程间通信机制的选择，是否存在比AF_UNIX更优的方案。

How fast are Linux pipes anyway?
In this post, we will explore how Unix pipes are implemented in Linux by iteratively optimizing a test program that writes and reads data through a pipe.
1
We will begin with a simple program with a throughput of around 3.5GiB/s, and improve its performance twentyfold. The improvements will be informed by profiling the program using Linuxâs
perf
tooling
.
2
The code
is available on GitHub
.
Chart showing the performance of our pipe test programs.
The post was inspired by reading
a highly optimized FizzBuzz program
, which pushes output to a pipe at a rate of ~35GiB/s on my laptop.
3
Our first goal will be to match that speed, explaining every step as we go along. Weâll also add an additional performance-improving measure, which is not needed in FizzBuzz since the bottleneck is actually computing the output, not IO, at least on my machine.
We will proceed as follows:
A first slow version of our pipe test bench;
How pipes are implemented internally, and why writing and reading from them is slow;
How the
vmsplice
and
splice
syscalls let us get around some (but not all!) of the slowness;
A description of Linux paging, leading up to a faster version using huge pages;
The final optimization, replacing polling with busy looping;
Some closing thoughts.
Section 4 is the heaviest on Linux kernel internals, so it might be interesting even if youâre familiar with the other topics treated in the post. For readers not familiar with the topics treated, only basic knowledge of C is assumed.
Letâs begin!
This will be similar in style to my
atan2f
performance investigation
, although the program in question will only be useful for learning.
Moreover, we will optimize code at a different level. While tuning
atan2f
consisted in micro-optimizations guided by the assembly output, tuning our pipe program will involve looking at
perf
events and reducing various sorts of kernel overhead.
â©ï¸
The tests were run on an Intel Skylake i7-8550U CPU, and on Linux 5.17.
Your mileage
will
vary, since the Linux internals that power the programs described in this post have been under constant change for the past couple of years, and will probably continue to be tweaked in future releases. Keep reading for more details!
â©ï¸
âFizzBuzzâ is an allegedly common coding interview question.
The details are not relevant to this blog post, but they are explained in the link. I have personally never been asked it, but I have it on good authority that it does happen!
â©ï¸
The challenge, and a slow first version
#
First of all, letâs start with measuring the performance of
the fabled FizzBuzz program
, following the rules laid down by the StackOverflow post:
% ./fizzbuzz | pv >/dev/null
422GiB 0:00:16 [36.2GiB/s]
pv
is âpipe viewerâ,
a handy utility
to measure the throughput of data flowing through a pipe. So
fizzbuzz
is producing output at a rate of 36GiB/s.
fizzbuzz
writes the output in blocks as big as the L2 cache, to strike a good balance between cheap access to memory and minimizing IO overhead.
On my machine, the L2 cache is 256KiB. Throughout this post, weâll also output blocks of 256KiB, but without âcomputingâ anything. Essentially, weâll try to measure the upper bound for programs writing to a pipe with a reasonable buffer size.
4
While
fizzbuzz
uses
pv
to measure speed, our setup will be slightly different: weâll implement the programs on both ends of the pipe. This is so that we fully control the code involved in pushing and pulling data from the pipe.
While we fix the buffer size, the numbers are actually not wildly different if we use different buffer sizes, given that other bottlenecks kick in.
â©ï¸
The code is available
in my
pipes-speed-test
repo
.
write.cpp
implements the writing, and
read.cpp
the reading.
write
repeatedly writes the same 256KiB forever.
read
reads through 10GiB of data and terminates, printing the throughput in GiB/s. Both executables accept a variety of command line options to change their behavior.
The first attempt at reading and writing from pipes will be using the
write
and
read
syscalls, using the same buffer size as
fizzbuzz
. Hereâs a view of the writing end:

>

data.title: How to negotiate your salary package
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
本文是工程师及其他专业人士的薪资谈判指南，特别针对认为谈判有道德问题的人。作者Patrick McKenzie（网名patio11）讲述了他撰写的一篇关于薪资谈判的文章，该文章已被数百万人阅读，并帮助许多人成功加薪，总金额达数千万美元。文章强调了谈判的重要性，并鼓励人们转变心态，接受谈判作为职业发展的一部分。

Patrick指出，谈判在求职前就已经开始，建议不要首先透露期望薪资，并强调研究和倾听对方信息的重要性。他鼓励利用新信息获取想要的结果，并使用多维度的偏好设置进行谈判。此外，Patrick提到，谈判不仅仅是技巧，还包含激励和劝说。文章最后由赞助商Mercury支持，Mercury为20多万家公司提供金融技术服务。

本文旨在帮助那些不常谈判或对此感到不适的人，通过具体例子和实用建议，让他们更自信地进行薪资谈判。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：薪资谈判策略的有效性，特别是在当前就业市场环境下

不同观点：
• **ryandrake** 认为Patrick的薪资谈判建议仅对行业内知名人士有效，普通员工很难成功谈判。他分享了自己25年职业生涯中谈判薪资屡屡失败的经历，并指出公司在面对普通候选人时往往没有太多协商空间。

• **neilv** 对Patrick的建议持怀疑态度，认为Patrick可能有足够的经济储备，且很久没有求职过。他暗示当前市场环境已经发生变化，Patrick的建议可能不再适用。

• **Sytten** 指出，随着大规模裁员和市场变化，工程师的议价能力已经大不如前。作为一家小 startup 的代表，他倾向于在招聘初期就明确薪资范围，以避免不必要的讨论。

• **RickS** 支持Patrick的建议，并分享了自己通过使用该建议获得显著职业提升的经历。他认为尽管市场环境有所变化，但薪资谈判仍然可行，并鼓励他人尝试。

• **andy99** 将薪资谈判比作在银行换汇，认为在一些大公司中，招聘人员的流程固定，谈判空间有限。只有在遇到真正的决策者时，谈判才有可能。

• **brunooliv** 表示自己因不擅长面试而难以获得多个offer进行谈判，认为市场环境和公司期望不现实。

• **wewewedxfgdf** 认为不先透露目标薪资会导致谈判失败，建议求职者应有明确的薪资目标。

• **dtnewman** 提供了一个Patrick多年前关于薪资谈判的文章链接，指出该讨论本质上是对该文章的音频化。

• **whiplash451** 认为自文章撰写以来，公司招聘的急迫性降低，导致文章中描述的许多机制失效。公司更倾向于等待招聘委员会对候选人产生强烈兴趣后再发offer。

• **VincentEvans** 关注加薪谈判的建议，询问是否有相关的可操作建议。

• **snowwrestler** 认为文章中关于工程师市场火热的观点可能已经过时，并指出新雇主可以通过数据共享服务获取候选人的前薪资，隐瞒前薪资并不会带来谈判优势。

• **cornhole** 主张可以一开始就要求一个很高的薪资，因为这样做没有成本或负面影响。

• **roland35** 认为谈判成功与否在开始之前就已决定，拥有备选offer和良好的面试表现是提高薪资的关键。

• **giantg2** 担心自己即将失业，并预期在当前市场下难以进行薪资谈判，可能会面临大幅减薪。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Patrick的薪资谈判建议在当前市场环境下的适用性，特别是对于普通员工和当前市场状况的变化。
- 不同观点还涉及谈判策略的实际操作性，包括是否应先透露目标薪资，以及在招聘流程中与谁谈判最有效。
- 一些人分享了个人成功或失败的经历，提供了对谈判过程的实际见解。

Until I ran
VaccinateCA

salary negotiation
. That essay has been read by millions of people. Of those people, a relatively small percentage send me email to tell me that the advice has worked for them. I previously kept a spreadsheet of the impact they shared with me, and it ticked over into eight figures of raises.

本文是工程师及其他专业人士的薪资谈判指南，特别针对认为谈判有道德问题的人。作者Patrick McKenzie（网名patio11）讲述了他撰写的一篇关于薪资谈判的文章，该文章已被数百万人阅读，并帮助许多人成功加薪，总金额达数千万美元。文章强调了谈判的重要性，并鼓励人们转变心态，接受谈判作为职业发展的一部分。

Patrick指出，谈判在求职前就已经开始，建议不要首先透露期望薪资，并强调研究和倾听对方信息的重要性。他鼓励利用新信息获取想要的结果，并使用多维度的偏好设置进行谈判。此外，Patrick提到，谈判不仅仅是技巧，还包含激励和劝说。文章最后由赞助商Mercury支持，Mercury为20多万家公司提供金融技术服务。

本文旨在帮助那些不常谈判或对此感到不适的人，通过具体例子和实用建议，让他们更自信地进行薪资谈判。

data.article_summary: Idle Reporter是一款帮助纽约市民举报商业车辆怠速问题的应用。它简化了投诉流程，用户可在5分钟内完成从录制到提交的全过程。主要功能包括时间戳相机、AI填表（需订阅）、手动编辑器、截图生成器和状态跟踪器。用户可保存报告并在合适时提交给DEP。需注意，该应用非官方工具，用户需自行确保报告的准确性。开发商Proof by Induction LLC不隶属于任何政府机构。应用大小45 MB，兼容iOS 17.0及以上版本，免费下载但提供内购订阅服务。

data.title: Show HN: A Tool to Summarize Kenya's Parliament with Rust, Whisper, and LLMs
data.author: collinsmuriuki
data.article_summary: Bunge Bits 是一个为肯尼亚国民议会和参议院会议提供简明摘要的平台，旨在提高立法信息的可访问性和易理解性，增强民主透明度，促进公民参与。该项目通过解析 YouTube 视频、使用数据库存储流数据、利用 OpenAI 的 Whisper 和 ChatGPT 4o 进行转录和摘要生成，并通过 Web 应用展示摘要内容。此外，项目还计划通过电子邮件发送新闻摘要，并寻求赞助以支持云基础设施和 API 使用。最终目标是帮助公民更好地参与民主进程，增强政治意识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）产品在实际应用中的潜力和具体使用案例，特别是在政治透明度和数据处理方面的应用。

不同观点：
• **对市场潜力的质疑**：[otherayden] 对LLM产品的市场需求表示好奇，想知道是否存在大规模市场，并询问是否可以分享使用数据以进一步了解。

• **技术解决方案的提供**：[sodality2] 提出可以通过本地托管转录来节省OpenAI的成本，并推荐使用其开发的工具mutter，方便自托管Whisper模型。

• **对实际应用价值的肯定**：[dr_kretyn] 认为LLM在揭示重要细节方面具有价值，特别是在法律和政策更新上，因为很多关键变化往往在讨论中被忽略或故意模糊。

• **类似项目的分享**：[jpmonette] 表示自己也在从事类似的地方议会项目，并对该项目表示赞赏。

• **详细案例的介绍**：[alexanderameye] 分享了其为比利时联邦议会创建的项目“zij werken voor u”，详细描述了从PDF抓取数据、解析、生成静态网站及构建搜索索引的整个过程，并提到自动化流程的实现。同时，建议创建一个汇总各国政治透明度公共项目的平台。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现细节**：[alexanderameye] 提到使用Rust脚本抓取PDF，使用Mistral进行总结，并将数据存储为.parquet文件。整个过程通过GitHub Actions自动化运行，最终成果展示在网站上，并通过Bluesky发布更新。

• **对改进官方网站的期望**：[alexanderameye] 希望比利时政府能够改进其现有的网站，提升其可用性。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中未见明显争议，但[otherayden]对LLM产品市场潜力的质疑与其他用户对实际应用价值的肯定形成对比，显示出对该技术应用前景的不同看法。

Bunge Bits
Bunge Bits provides convenient summaries of Kenyan National Assembly and Senate proceedings, making legislative information more accessible and digestible.
Motivations
The driving force behind Bunge Bits is to strengthen Kenya's democracy by making legislative processes more transparent and understandable to all citizens. The aim is to bridge the gap between complex government proceedings and the average Kenyan, fostering increased civic engagement and political awareness. By offering concise, easy-to-digest summaries of legislative sessions, I hope to empower citizens with the knowledge they need to participate more fully in their democracy, hold elected officials accountable, and engage in informed discussions about the issues that affect their lives.
Ultimately, Bunge Bits seeks to contribute to a more engaged, informed, and participatory democratic process in Kenya.

data.title: I was surprised by how simple an allocator is
data.author: gilgamesh3
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了编写内存分配器的基础知识，并以简单的分配器实现为例，特别提到了伙伴系统（Buddy System）。文章首先指出开发者希望在mimalloc中预分配内存的需求，并通过自行实现一个简单的内存分配器来解决该问题。作者解释了内存分配器的作用，包括内存的分配、重新分配和释放，并讨论了内存碎片化问题，包括内部和外部碎片化。伙伴系统作为一种简单可靠的分配技术被详细介绍，其通过递归地将内存块一分为二来满足分配请求。分配和释放内存的操作都相对直接，主要是分裂和合并内存块。最终，作者对其简单实现感到惊讶，并计划将其用于mimalloc的预分配内存功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：内存分配器的设计与使用在不同系统中的重要性及其实现难度

不同观点：
• [b0a04gl] 认为内存分配器的选择对系统性能至关重要，特别是在像Unity和嵌入式系统中，选择不当可能导致帧丢失或严重bug。不同的场景（如实时系统、基础设施）需要不同的分配策略，通用分配器无法满足所有需求。Rust中的分配抽象主要是为了处理内存生命周期和所有权问题，且如`Bumpalo`这样的分配器在特定场景下非常有用。
• [romesmoke] 指出，分配器的设计，尤其是策略和政策部分，非常复杂。尽管编写一个简单的分配器不难，但设计一个在各种情况下都能高效运行的分配器非常具有挑战性。特别是面对不确定的对象大小和生命周期时，分配器可能表现不佳。因此，通用解决方案在实践中往往不够理想。
• [wavemode] 对原文试图传达的观点（编写分配器不难）表示怀疑，认为虽然像mimalloc这样的分配器代码量不大，但这并不能充分证明编写一个好的分配器是容易的。
• [GuB-42] 认为编写一个基础的分配器不难，但编写一个好的分配器则需要丰富的实际系统知识和经验。
• [the__alchemist] 分享了在嵌入式Rust项目中不使用分配器而遭遇内存不足的问题，指出大多数流行的protobuf库和ESP都依赖分配器，而使用无分配器的方案（如Heapless）可能导致内存紧张。
• [jasonthorsness] 主张应用更多专用内存分配器，因为针对特定使用模式设计分配器可以简化内存管理，特别是在使用模式可预测的情况下。然而，在高层次语言中实现这一点非常困难。
• [AndyKelley] 提供了一个简短的线程安全分配器示例，展示了编写一个简单的分配器是可行的。
• [notepad0x90] 关注内存管理内核子系统的复杂性，特别是关于固定页面大小的使用，并提问是否存在不使用固定页面大小的简单内存管理方案。
• [userbinator] 赞同分配器可以很简单，并指出一个基础的first-fit分配器可以非常短小高效，利用空闲空间存储元数据也是一种简单有效的优化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是编写一个好的内存分配器是否困难。虽然基础分配器的实现不难，但设计一个能在各种实际场景中高效运行的分配器需要深厚的专业知识和经验。
• 另一个值得注意的点是专用分配器和通用分配器之间的对比，专用分配器在特定场景下表现更好，而通用分配器则难以应对所有情况。
• 讨论中还涉及了内存管理内核子系统的设计，特别是关于动态页面大小的可行性和复杂性。

44315968.article_content:
Table of Contents
Introduction
Memory allocators
Buddy system
Allocation
Deallocation
Introduction
Recently I was looking at an issue on
mimalloc
, a "
state-of-the-art
" memory allocator developed by Microsoft.
The issue
was quite simple, developers wanted a way to preallocate a piece of memory and use it as mimalloc's heap. Seeing that
mimalloc
does not offer this feature, I thought:
"
how hard can it be to write a memory allocator to manage a preallocated region?
".
The answer to this question is:
"
given enough time, even a monkey with a typewriter can write a memory allocator
".
The implementation is around 163 LoC and very straightforward.
Memory allocators
To write a memory allocator, we first need to understand what an allocator does. An allocator is "
a component of a programming language or runtime system that is responsible for managing the allocation and deallocation of memory during program execution
".
1
Roughly speaking, a custom allocator needs to provide a way for the developer to allocate, deallocate and reallocate memory from the operating system.
The C standard library provides
malloc/free/resize
(
C11 introduced
aligned_alloc
and C23 introduced
free_sized
and
free_aligned_sized
), then a custom allocator will need to provide the same (
or nearly
) the same interface for easy integration with already existing code.
Memory Fragmentation
One of the problems an allocator tries to solve is memory fragmentation. Memory fragmentation happens when the memory is split into small unused blocks throughout a memory chunk, making larger allocations harder because there is fewer contiguous memory available to allocate.
Since memory is allocated in chunks, sometimes the real size allocated by the allocator is bigger than the requested size, and the unused memory left is wasted. This is called
internal fragmentation
2
.
External fragmentation
"arises when free memory is separated into small blocks and is interspersed by allocated memory"
3
.
There are a lot of methods an allocator can use to minimize memory fragmentation. General purpose ones do it by creating different allocation buckets based on the allocation size. So if an allocation of 512 bytes is requested, the allocator will use a bucket for small allocations, preventing that 512 bytes are wasted in the memory when big allocations happen.
Buddy system
There are various allocation techniques, and one of the simplest and most reliable is the buddy allocation, which is the one I implemented. It is widely used in the industry, and it is the one used by the Linux kernel to handle page allocations (
albeit a modified version
).
The way it works is by dividing a contiguous memory chunk into two smaller chunks of memory, each a power of two (
hence the "buddy"
), until a small enough size is reached, and then returning this memory to the user.
Allocation
As an example, suppose the programmer requested a 16KB memory chunk, and the size of the whole memory block is 256KB. It will do:
Requested size is smaller than the chunk size, it will split the 256KB chunk into two 128KB chunk.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 128KB chunk is split in two 64KB chunk.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 64KB chunk is split in two 32KB chunks.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 32KB chunk is split in two 16KB chunks.
Requested size is equals the chunk size. Return it to the user.
Here is the representation of this allocation:
And that is it, just split the memory until the requested size is
<=
than the current chunk size. The disadvantage of this technique is that it has internal fragmentation since the returned chunk can be smaller than the requested size and so the unused memory is wasted.
Deallocation
To deallocate the memory is straightforward, just mark the chunk received by the
free
function as unused and check if its buddy is also unused, if it is, just coalesce it into a bigger chunk.
Suppose the previous 16KB memory chunk allocated is being freed, it would be like this
4
:
Resize
The resize part is also simple to implement, and it stays as a exercise for the reader.
Conclusion
After spending some time reading and implementing an allocator, I was surprised by how simple an allocator is. Even general purpose allocators like
mimalloc
is only a few thousand lines of code and most of that code is (
probaly
) just dealing with multithread.
The code for my implementation can be found here:
tgmatos/imalloc
I would have loved to delve more into the internals of an allocator, the techniques general purpose allocators use and everything, but I have neither the time nor the proficiency (
yet
) to write an article about it. I will probably do it in the future, but for now my plan is to just implement a way for mimalloc to use preallocated memory.
1
Definition taken from
What’s a Memory Allocator anyway ?
2
Internal Memory Fragmentation (wikipedia)
3
External Memory Fragmentation (wikipedia)
4
Sinc

data.title: AGI is Mathematically Impossible 2: When Entropy Returns
data.author: ICBTheory
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）系统的理论限制和信息熵在复杂决策空间中的行为。

不同观点：
• ICBTheory认为，AGI系统在某些语义条件下会由于熵的行为而崩溃，称之为IOpenER理论。该观点得到了Apple研究的支持，但作者声称这并非针对Apple的研究而作。
• viralsink指出，AGI面临的问题类似于人类认知的局限性，即在无限解空间中依赖启发法。他还提到了计算不可约性问题，认为这是AGI面临的另一个障碍。
• Animats认为，Roger Penrose在三十年前已经提出了类似的观点，并且在AI发展良好之前更有说服力。
• tim333对该论文持怀疑态度，认为基于人类神经网络模拟的AGI不太可能面临如论文所述的根本性问题。
• kelseyfrog批评论文回避了关键问题，特别是关于人类智能是否可以被形式化的问题，认为这是一种逃避。
• proc0认为论文跳过了对AI的定义，直接讨论AGI，并质疑是否所有AI实现都可以被图灵机模拟。
• daedrdev认为自然界避免了熵陷阱问题，通过复制自然选择，AI模型也可以避免。
• cainxinth指出，论文对AGI的定义过于严格，认为即使不完美的系统也可以被称为AGI。
• like_any_other质疑人类大脑是否超越数学，或者人类是否并非普遍智能。
• moktonar认为问题归结为是否存在有效的算法来模拟量子物理，这决定了AGI是否可能。
• predrag_peter区分了AI的复杂性和人类智能的不可还原性，认为将两者混淆是不明智的。
• adamnemecek仅表示对论文的呈现方式感到反感。
• agitracking对人类智能是否可以映射到数学表示好奇，并提到相关讨论的时机有趣。
• weregiraffe直接称论文为“江湖骗术”。
• furyofantares以幽默方式表达对论文某些部分的不满，但询问其他人是否认为论文有价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AGI系统的理论限制，特别是熵增问题是否会导致系统崩溃。
• 对人类智能是否可以被形式化以及是否可以被完全模拟存在不同看法。
• 对论文的定义和论证方式存在质疑，尤其是其对AGI的严格定义和跳过AI定义直接讨论AGI的做法。
• 讨论中多次提到计算不可约性和量子物理模拟问题，认为这些是AGI发展的潜在障碍。

总体而言，讨论围绕AGI的理论可行性及其面临的数学和物理限制展开，存在多种观点和批评。

• **jmward01** 指出火山的喷发活动具有规律性，并引用了Geology Hub对之前喷发事件的报道，暗示对火山活动有可预测性。
• **dluan** 关注火山喷发对空气质量的影响，特别是Oahu岛的VOG（火山烟雾）问题，表达了对风向变化的担忧。
• **1970-01-01** 对直播链接表示失望，认为没有值得看的内容，只有蒸汽。
• **dboreham** 以幽默的方式提到自己似乎能“终止”火山喷发，通过个人经历调侃了火山活动的不可预测性。
• **snvzz** 对火山喷发的时机提出疑问，提到“最近的轰炸”，暗示可能对火山喷发与人类活动之间的关系存在质疑。
• **Eduard** 寻求具体时间戳，以观看“超过1000英尺高的熔岩”，显示出对特定喷发场景的兴趣。
• **ganeshkrishnan** 详细描述了大岛的多样气候带和自然景观，分享了一次独特的公共汽车旅行体验，突显了大岛的自然和人文魅力。

补充讨论：
• 火山活动的实时观测与信息获取是讨论的核心，asix66和1970-01-01的观点形成对比，一个提供信息源，另一个则对信息内容不满。
• 旅游体验是另一个重要讨论点，jasonthorsness和ganeshkrishnan都分享了个人经历，但前者关注火山本身，后者强调大岛的整体自然和人文景观。
• dluan和jmward01提到了火山喷发对环境和气候的影响，前者担心空气质量，后者指出喷发规律性。
• snvzz的评论引发对火山喷发时机与人类活动的关联的思考，尽管未展开详细讨论。

争议焦点：
• 直播视频的实用性是争议的一个焦点，1970-01-01认为没有看点，而asix66则提供了信息来源。
• 火山喷发时机与人类活动的潜在关联（snvzz的评论）可能引发更多讨论，但未在对话中深入展开。

data.title: Discover C++26's compile-time reflection
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: Herb Sutter宣布，C++26将引入编译时反射功能。反射允许程序访问代码结构，例如列举类的方法。与大多数编程语言的运行时反射不同，C++引入的是编译时反射，这将显著提升性能。这一特性将应用于像simdjson这样的库，实现数据结构与JSON之间的高效转换，无需样板代码。此外，编译时反射还能简化对象到SQL的映射，通过单一函数调用生成SQL插入语句。尽管示例代码看起来复杂，但它展示了C++26中编译时反射的强大和高效，未来将广泛应用于各种项目简化与优化中。
