主要讨论点：C++新特性（特别是编译时反射和与标准库的绑定）的引入及其影响

不同观点：
• [npalli] 支持新提案，认为新提案中的例子对未来使用有帮助，特别是对于STL和编译器内部状态的绑定。链接了一个标准提案文档，供他人参考。

• [112233] 反对新特性的引入，认为这将加剧编译器内部状态与标准模板库（STL）的绑定，使得不依赖标准库的C++项目越来越难以维持。特别提到初始化列表、RTTI以及协程等特性，认为这些使得不使用标准库的嵌入式项目变得更加困难，感觉C++正在背离其非标准库使用的实践。

• [jandrewrogers] 支持编译时反射的引入，认为这将显著增强C++的元编程能力，尽管C++在语法美观性上表现不佳，新语法丑陋但实用。

• [izger] 认为C++的语法越来越晦涩，建议通过基本的C++语法在编译时实现模板编程，并将其纳入标准库。

• [jasonthorsness] 认为新特性的复杂性可能会被封装在库中，尽管使用上可能有挑战，但支持C++在消除不必要的运行时工作方面的努力。

• [mystified5016] 对新语法持批评态度，认为其过于怪异，甚至比Perl还复杂，虽然C++终于引入了反射，但已经晚了数十年。表示越来越倾向于使用纯C而非C++，并提出使用C#生成C代码的替代方案。

• [MoonGhost] 建议创建一个更人性化的C++薄包装语言，使其具有相同特性但更易读，并能双向直接翻译。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于C++新特性的复杂性和语法美观性，特别是编译时反射和与标准库的绑定是否必要和实用。
• 一些开发者担心这些新特性会使得C++变得更加晦涩和难以维护，特别是对于嵌入式项目和不使用标准库的项目。
• 支持者认为新特性增强了C++的元编程能力，有助于优化程序性能。
• 有建议提出创建更易读的C++变体或使用其他语言生成C代码的替代方案。

Herb Sutter just announced
that the verdict is in: C++26, the next version of C++, will include
compile-time
reflection.
Reflection in programming languages means that you have access the code’s own structure. For example, you can take a class, and enumerate its methods. For example, you could receive a class, check whether it contains a method that returns a string, call this method and get the string. Most programming languages have some form of reflection. For example, the good old Java does have complete reflection support.
However, C++ is getting compile-time reflection. It is an important development.
I announced a few months ago that thanks to joint work with Francisco Geiman Thiesen,
the performance-oriented JSON library simdjson would support compile-time reflection
as soon as mainstream compilers support it.
This allows you to take your own data structure and convert it to a JSON string without any effort, and at high speed:
kid k{12, "John", {"car", "ball"}};
simdjson::to_json(k);
// would generate {"age": 12, "name": "John", "toys": ["car", "ball"]}
And you can also go back, given a JSON document, you can get back an instance of your custom type:
kid k = doc.get<kid>();
The code can be highly optimized and it can be thoroughly tested, in the main library. Removing the need for boilerplate code has multiple benefits.

data.author: albert_e

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何恢复长时间专注阅读的能力

不同观点：
• LeonardoTolstoy认为，通过阅读轻松的虚构作品，如幻想或科幻小说，可以重新培养阅读的乐趣和专注力。他强调通过简单的阅读练习来恢复阅读能力，类似于应对写作障碍的建议——“ just write!”。
• ranger207支持通过逐步增加阅读时间来恢复阅读习惯，建议从吸引人的虚构作品开始，而不是必须阅读的材料，如技术手册。
• treetalker提出了一种更为严谨的阅读方法，建议在阅读时手中拿着铅笔，重述并重写所读内容，以加深理解和批判性思维。他还推荐了Mortimer Adler的《如何阅读一本书》作为参考。
• kentich推荐使用黑屏软件（如Black Screen）来间隔休息，以提高专注力，并建议根据疲劳程度调整间隔时间。
• codingdave建议回归传统的书本阅读，避免电子书的干扰，并通过设定研究目标来增强阅读的持久力。
• sandreas认为消除电子设备的干扰，并强迫自己阅读超过20分钟以进入心流状态是有效的。
• mc3301强调了良好的睡眠习惯和选择有趣的读物，如漫画小说，以重新激发阅读兴趣。
• sn9建议通过冥想、避免屏幕时间和保证健康生活方式来提高专注力。
• firefax提出戒酒可能有助于改善生活方式和阅读习惯。
• kylecazar认为选择性阅读和认真阅读是关键，避免随意点击和浏览多篇文章。
• Haeuserschlucht认为大多数文本写得不好，缺乏情感，因此不如虚构作品吸引人，这可能是阅读困难的原因。
• jvanderbot建议减少生活中的刺激以提高专注力，类似于“多巴胺饮食”的概念。
• helph67引用了2017年的一项研究，指出大声朗读有助于记忆。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenCitations工具的使用、数据来源、技术实现以及与区块链的潜在关系

不同观点：
• **ks2048**：建议显示所输入DOI的完整引用信息，并质疑OpenCitations如何填充其数据。他提到自己尝试的一个例子中，论文有30多篇参考文献，但工具只显示了9篇。
   
• **avoutos**：认为该工具可能对快速引用有帮助，但更推荐使用像Zotero这样成熟的开源引用管理器，暗示该工具在功能上可能不如专业的管理器全面。

• **oersted**：对工具背后的技术实现感兴趣，询问是否使用了开源库或能否描述所用的方法。他提到自己曾研究过从论文PDF中提取特征的相关问题，认为工具的实现方式值得分享和学习。他还建议增加一个“关于”页面以增加透明度。

• **BSOhealth**：关注DOI与区块链的交互，提出是否需要使用区块链来解决学术出版物的来源问题，认为这是一个值得探索的应用场景，但同时也对当前区块链的实际价值持怀疑态度。

• **技术透明性**：oersted强调了对工具技术实现的兴趣以及对“关于”页面的需求，显示出用户对工具背后技术细节和透明度的关注。

• **数据完整性**：ks2048对OpenCitations数据的不完整性提出了质疑，反映出用户对工具数据准确性和全面性的关注。

主要讨论点：美国邮政服务（USPS）的电动邮政车辆项目被取消及其相关争议

不同观点：
• **对项目取消的批评**：
  - [i80and] 认为取消项目是愚蠢的行为，质疑谁会大规模购买这些定制的邮政车辆，因为市场可能无法吸收这些特殊用途的车辆。
  - [spike021] 从邮递员的工作环境角度出发，指出新车辆能极大改善工作条件，尤其是在高温环境下。
  - [dyauspitr] 强调邮政工作人员喜欢这种新设计，并且这些车辆运行和清洁成本更低，对环境更友好。
  - [candiddevmike] 提到这些车辆是由Oshkosh Corporation制造的，是近年来公共/私人合作 redesign 中较为成功的案例之一，威斯康星州居民应该对此感到愤怒。

• **对项目取消的支持或中立态度**：
  - [tlogan] 指出实际上只有93辆电动汽车被交付，远低于预期的3000辆，认为大规模取消的标题可能更吸引眼球，但实际上影响有限。
  - [SoftTalker] 认为取消项目可能是基于“沉没成本谬误”的考虑，尽管初期成本已经发生，但如果未来这些定制电动车的成本高于标准商用车辆，那么取消可能有其合理性。

• **对争议的反思和扩展**：
  - [CoastalCoder] 请求了解共和党支持取消项目的最佳理由，表示愿意在做出判断前听取双方意见。
  - [dang] 提到 proposed bills 通常不会成为好的讨论话题，因为大多数时候并不会产生实际结果，并表示对具体法案不了解。

补充讨论：
• [NewJazz] 提供了另一个无付费墙的故事链接，供大家参考。
• [faraggi] 直接抨击决策者腐败和无用，没有提供具体论据。

争议的焦点：
- 项目取消是否合理，特别是考虑到已经发生的成本和未来运营的经济性。
- 电动邮政车辆对邮递员工作环境的改善和环保效益是否足以支持继续该项目。
- 共和党取消项目的动机和其合理性。

data.title: 2048 with only 64 bits of state
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 《Bitwise Challenge: 2048》是一个在终端运行的经典2048游戏实现。该项目将整个游戏板状态压缩到仅64位，允许通过一个数字分享游戏状态。若环境变量`$STATE`未设置，则游戏会生成一个随机种子，开始新的游戏；若设置了`$STATE`，则游戏状态和后续生成单元都是确定的。项目主要使用Shell语言编写，目前获得60个星标和1个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：2048游戏的64位状态实现及其技术细节

不同观点：
• [eurleif] 认为实现的亮点在于用不到200行的bash脚本完成，而不是64位状态的实现。他解释了用4位可以表示一个格子的12种可能状态（包括空格），从而总状态可以用64位表示。
• [rossant] 建议将其实现为一个C语言函数`int64 run_2048(int64 state, int input)`，将状态和输入（上下左右）作为参数，返回新的状态，认为这可以作为一个有趣的代码高尔夫练习。
• [lotyrin] 强调了将复杂状态空间映射到简单线性序列的技巧，并举例说明如何将有限字符集编码映射到数字序列中，认为这是很多人忽略的技巧。
• [bvanderveen] 赞赏了简洁的实现，但指出了一个bug：使用“角策略”时，有时左上角的格子会随机变小。
• [nneonneo] 分享了类似的技巧，其2048 AI允许格子达到32768，并使用每个半字节表示一个格子，从而将整个游戏板打包到一个寄存器中。
• [carra] 提到原版2048游戏在达到2048后仍可继续，而该实现为了实现64位状态去掉了这一选项，但仍认为这是一个聪明的实现。

补充讨论：
• [enriquto] 通过数学计算论证了在不超过2048的情况下，总状态数为11^16，约需要56位，因此64位是足够的，认为这是一个紧凑的实现。
• [Normal_gaussian] 和 [meta-level] 没有直接讨论技术细节，而是提到安装命令和自己的bash脚本，更多是表达对该实现的兴趣或对比自己的经验。
• [kinduff] 简单赞赏了代码行数和实现的聪明。
• [mark_undoio] 表达了对作者的赞赏和对其创造力的惊讶。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于实现中的潜在bug，[bvanderveen] 指出的“角策略”问题是否存在及如何修复。
• 另一个讨论点是64位状态实现的实际限制和原版游戏的差异。

data.title: The cultural decline of literary fiction
data.author: libraryofbabel
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：当代文学小说为何不再像经典作品那样受欢迎

不同观点：
• **经典作品的持续影响力**：
  - [jl6] 认为，像《傲慢与偏见》、《战争与和平》等经典作品每年仍售出成千上万册，新书必须与这些已存在的作品竞争，而消费者的注意力和时间有限，导致新书较难取代经典。
  - [libraryofbabel] 补充，人们依然阅读具有挑战性的文学小说，只是作者多为已故之人，这对当代文学小说作家来说是个打击。

• **当代文学与"类型小说"的界限**：
  - [pclmulqdq] 指出，如今被视为"文学"的作品在19世纪可能是通俗读物，因此不应轻易将当代流行读物视为"低俗"。
  - [libraryofbabel] 也提到，文学小说与"类型小说"的界限未必明确，Ursula Le Guin 就是很好的反例。

• **文化与市场变化的影响**：
  - [mslansn] 认为，当前存在对非白人男性作家的过度推崇，不论其作品质量如何，这影响了市场选择。
  - [ang_cire] 强调，批评家与消费者之间的脱节使得许多行业难以重新盈利，尤其是在当前经济环境下。

• **阅读习惯与媒介变化**：
  - [dfedbeef] 认为，讲故事的方式已经改变，文学小说作家面临困境是因为他们固守纸质媒介。
  - [perching_aix] 表示，阅读变得低效且不舒适，宁愿选择其他更方便的媒介。
  - [Ekaros] 提出，文化更加碎片化，其他媒介（如电视剧）提供了类似的体验，削弱了小说在这方面的需求。

• **社会与教育因素**：
  - [amanaplanacanal] 认为，反智主义的上升和人文学科教育的衰退（因经济和国家安全驱动）可能导致文学小说读者的减少。

补充讨论：
• **作家与市场成功**：
  - [mcnamaratw] 讨论了对实验性作家的阅读体验，并提到像Sally Rooney这样的作家为何能取得商业成功是一个值得探讨的问题。
  
• **文化地位的变化**：
  - [fullshark] 指出，拥有对文化 artifact X 的意见不再赋予个人地位，因为太多人有意见但未对社会做出实际贡献。
  
• **个人经历与偏见**：
  - [kayodelycaon] 认为，现代文学小说的自命不凡让人反感，尤其是被教育体系强迫接受这种作品。

争议焦点：
• 当代文学小说与类型小说的价值之争，以及市场推广对作家成功的影响。

data.title: Why do all browsers' user agents start with "Mozilla/"? (2008)
data.author: nan60
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户代理字符串（User-Agent）的历史、用途及其存在的问题

不同观点：
• **[gnabgib]** 通过列出多个相关讨论链接，指出User-Agent字符串的问题在过去几年中反复出现，并受到社区关注。这表明该话题具有一定的历史延续性和讨论热度。

• **[impure]** 提出一种讽刺性建议，认为Mozilla可以通过对使用Mozilla开头的用户代理字符串收费来解决资金问题，暗示当前User-Agent系统的混乱和不必要性。

• **[technothrasher]** 指出并非所有浏览器都遵循常见的User-Agent格式，例如Lynx浏览器，以此来说明User-Agent字符串的多样性和复杂性。

• **[RainyDayTmrw]** 将User-Agent字符串的问题与Windows没有Windows 9版本类比，暗示命名和兼容性问题的存在可能是由于历史和技术上的复杂性。

• **[anamexis]** 提出一个实验性问题，询问如果使用一个通用的User-Agent字符串，现代浏览器会有多少功能失效或降级，以此探讨User-Agent字符串的实际必要性。

• **[dankwizard]** 认为当前User-Agent字符串主要被用于伪装成其他浏览器或进行不正当行为，建议废弃这一机制，反映了User-Agent系统的滥用问题。

• **[usr1106]** 分享了个人经历，指出由于Cloudflare的限制，真实Mozilla衍生浏览器无法访问某些网站，表明User-Agent字符串在实际使用中可能导致合法用户被误拦。

• **[shmerl]** 认为User-Agent字符串的问题源于奇怪且复杂的理由，并质疑为何从未被修正或重新命名，表达了对当前命名系统的不满。

• **[nreilly]** 以讽刺口吻建议采用类似termcap的系统来处理浏览器兼容性问题，暗示需要一种更合理和标准化的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• User-Agent字符串的滥用和复杂性是讨论的核心，包括其在兼容性伪装、历史遗留问题和技术滥用方面的表现。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该废弃或改革User-Agent字符串机制，以解决其带来的各种问题。
• 个人经历和具体案例（如Cloudflare的拦截问题）为讨论提供了现实依据，显示了User-Agent字符串在实际应用中的影响。
• 一些参与者提出了替代方案或类比，以探讨更有效的技术解决方案。

data.title: What would happen if you tried to land on a gas giant?
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了关于木星和土星等气态巨行星的最新研究和发现。气态巨行星主要由氢和氦组成，形成过程主要有两种理论：核吸积和盘不稳定性。核吸积指尘埃和岩石等较重粒子聚集后吸附周围气体形成行星，而盘不稳定性则认为行星通过气体和尘埃团的直接凝结快速形成。气态巨行星没有固体表面，大气层逐渐变薄，内部有极高温和高压。木星和土星的结构复杂，可能拥有模糊或扩散的核心，并且存在如木星大红斑般的剧烈风暴。这些新发现改变了科学家对气态巨行星的理解，并有助于设计未来的探测任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕木星及其卫星的物理特性、探索潜力以及人类太空探索的未来发展方向

不同观点：
• [notepad0x90] 认为木星的液态核心和气态质量之间的某处可能存在固态金属和物质，并提出木星的强大磁场可能与内部热液流动有关。他还主张，相比火星，木星及其卫星（如木卫三和欧罗巴）更适合人类探索，因为它们有水和磁场，可以减少辐射。他批评当前太空探索过于注重科学实验，而忽视实际应用，如建立月球基地或太空定居点。他呼吁人类应更具冒险精神，发展核动力推进等技术，以加快太空探索的步伐。

• [chasil] 回应了关于木星内部构成的猜测，特别提到了“金属氢”的可能性，并引用了维基百科的相关资料以支持其观点。

• [rybosome] 提出了一个假设场景：身穿普通太空服的人在接近木星大气层时会如何死亡。他认为，木星上层大气中超过300英里每小时的强风会是最先致命的因素，早于高压、高温和腐蚀性物质。

• [fmajid] 简短地指出，试图登陆像木星这样的气态巨行星就像试图登陆云朵一样不切实际，暗示木星不适合登陆探索。

补充讨论：
• [notepad0x90] 进一步讨论了人类太空探索的潜力，强调了木星卫星上的资源（如水）和减少辐射的优势，并批评当前太空项目缺乏实际应用和长远规划。他以木星探测和土星冰环为例，说明太空资源可以为人类所用。

• 争议的焦点在于人类太空探索的优先目标。有人认为应优先探索和利用木星系统，而不是火星，这与当前主流的火星探索计划形成对比。此外，关于如何在技术风险和探索收益之间取得平衡也存在讨论。

• 对于木星内部构成和环境条件的科学猜测和假设也是讨论的重要部分，包括金属氢的存在和木星大气中的极端条件。

44349662.article_content:
This striking view of Jupiter's Great Red Spot and turbulent southern hemisphere was captured by NASA's Juno spacecraft as it performed a close pass of the gas giant planet.
Image: NASA
Get the Popular Science daily newsletter💡
Breakthroughs, discoveries, and DIY tips sent every weekday.
Email address
Sign up
Thank you!
Terms of Service
and
Privacy Policy.
Our solar system contains three types of planets. Between the four terrestrial planets–Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars–and the distant ice giants of Neptune and Uranus, sit two gas giants: Saturn and Jupiter.
These planets are mostly composed of hydrogen and helium gas. Researchers now appreciate that gas planets are more complex than first thought. New findings have implications for our understanding of how these planets formed and will help design future missions to potentially visit them.
How do gas giants form?
Gas giants originate from one of two processes. The first method is called
core accretion
, explains
Ravit Helled
, a professor of theoretical astrophysics at the University of Zürich. This starts with the birth of a new star, when molecular clouds collapse under gravitational pressure. Whorls of gas–called protoplanetary disks–start to spin around these new stars. Within these gas disks will be heavier particles–dust, rock, or any elements heavier than helium. These particles can clump together and then suck in gas from the surrounding disk, forming a giant planet mainly composed of gas.
A second method that may form gas giants called
disk instability
–this is a newer theory that still causes some controversy among planetary theorists. According to this idea, when massive protoplanetary disks cool down, they become unstable and can produce clumps of rock and gas that evolve into gas giants. Importantly, this proposed formation process happens much more quickly than
core accretion
. Helled says that Saturn and Jupiter likely formed via core accretion, but that disk instability may “explain very massive planets at large orbits or giant planets around small mass stars.”
Landing on a gas giant
Regardless of how they form, the structure of gas giants is nothing like that of terrestrial planets like Earth.
Jupiter
and Saturn don’t have a surface in the same way Earth does. Instead, their atmosphere simply gets thinner until there isn’t enough density left to call the surrounding air part of the planet anymore. “There is no location where you can say, okay, this is where the planet stops,” says Helled.
A spaceship attempting to “land” on Jupiter’s “surface” would have to overcome some significant obstacles. Once you enter the cloud of gas that roughly marks the beginning of a giant like Jupiter, temperature and pressure steadily increase as your head toward the planet’s core, and gaseous hydrogen and helium morph into liquid form. While our solar system’s gas giants are far from the sun, the core of a gas giant is likely to be incredibly hot–Jupiter’s is
estimated
at around 43,000 degrees Fahrenheit. You’d also have to pass through the thick clouds of ammonia found in Jupiter’s upper atmosphere.
If you make your ship from tough stuff–tougher than any known substance on Earth–that could survive these conditions, it might make it to a gas giant’s core. What it would find there in the alien murk is still unclear.
“For decades, it was assumed that there was a defined core,” says Helled. Recent probe missions, like
Juno
and
Cassini
, have orbited Jupiter and Saturn, respectively. The information these probes sent back has changed that view.
On September 15, 2017, Cassini plunged into Saturn’s atmosphere as a final mission. Artist illustration of the spacecraft’s final moments.
Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech
NASA/JPL-Caltech
“We now think that they have what we call
fuzzy
or diluted cores,” says Helled. This means that there isn’t a clear transition point between the upper layers of liquid gas and liquid hydrogen and helium and the planet’s core.
In truth,
Juno
and
Cassini’s data
has revolutionized our understanding of these planet’s structures. Helled explains that they likely have complex heat and composition gradients. Jupiter is famously wracked with massive storms, like the
Great Red Spot
, which produces winds up to 425 mph (640 km/h). Some of these shifts can produce dramatic phenomena. Jupiter and Saturn likely have regions in which helium gas separates from hydrogen. Here, the helium becomes a rain of droplets that pour towards the planet’s core.
These insights can reveal more about our solar system’s giants, as well as similar planets outside our solar system.
“Now we realize that some of the simple assumptions that we’ve made to model these planets are wrong, and we need to modify the models,” says Helled.
This story is part of Popular Science’s
Ask Us Anything series
, where we answer your most outlandish, mind-burning questions, from the ordinary to the off-the-wall. Have something you’ve always wanted to know?

.

data.title: We’ve had a Denisovan skull since the 1930s, only nobody knew
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 2021年研究发现，出土于中国哈尔滨的14.6万年前的头骨属于丹尼索瓦人。最初该头骨被认为属于新物种**Homo longi**（龙人），但蛋白质分析显示其与丹尼索瓦人的蛋白质序列相匹配，证实其实为丹尼索瓦人。这一发现为了解神秘的丹尼索瓦人相貌提供了重要线索。头骨在1930年代出土后被隐藏多年，直到2018年才交给科学家研究。尽管**Homo longi**的分类曾有争议，新证据表明其应归为丹尼索瓦人，解决了长久以来的谜题。丹尼索瓦人作为我们祖先的“幽灵谱系”，因缺乏完整化石而长期神秘莫测，哈尔滨头骨的发现让我们首次清晰看到了这一古人类的面貌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Harbin头骨及多地区进化假说的讨论

不同观点：
• [AlotOfReading] 提供了对多地区进化假说的背景介绍，指出中国科学院一些学者长期主张这一假说，认为现代中国人是从中国境内的古老人类进化而来的。每隔几年，他们就会挖出一组具有奇特形态的骨头，赋予新的名称，并声称这是新的缺失环节。AlotOfReading认为，这篇论文的结果坚定地支持了西方共识，即现代人类并非通过多地区进化独立演化，同时也支持了关于丹尼索瓦人广泛分布的推测，开启了许多未来的研究方向。

• [poulpy123] 对点击诱饵式标题表达不满，虽然没有深入讨论研究内容，但表现出对标题党的不满情绪。

• [adampwells] 提供了一个相关文章链接，但没有进一步阐述自己的观点或立场，可能是为了引导读者查看更多信息。

• [pyman] 通过一个个人故事，回忆起发现旧存储盘的经历，间接提到一些与古人类研究无关但涉及技术与时间流逝的问题，未直接参与主要讨论。

• [ldjkfkdsjnv] 简短地提到“古老的DNA中隐藏着黑暗的真相”，暗示对古代DNA研究可能揭示未知或有争议的历史真相，但未具体说明。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在中国多地区进化假说的有效性上。AlotOfReading明确指出，这项研究结果支持西方主流观点，即现代人类起源的“走出非洲”理论，而非多地区进化假说。

• 不同评论者对讨论的参与度各异，有些提供了实质性论据和例子（如AlotOfReading），而有些则表达了个人情绪或提供了额外阅读资源。

A
146,000-year-old skull from Harbin, China,
belongs to a Denisovan, according to a recent study of proteins preserved inside the ancient bone. The paleoanthropologists who studied the Harbin skull in 2021 declared it a new (to us) species,
Homo longi
. But the Harbin skull still contains enough of its original proteins to tell a different story: A few of them matched specific proteins from Denisovan bones and teeth, as encoded in Denisovan DNA.
So
Homo longi
was a Denisovan all along, and thanks to the remarkably well-preserved skull, we finally know what the enigmatic Denisovans actually looked like.
Credit:
Ni et al. 2021
The Harbin skull (left) and the Dali skull (right).
Unmasking Dragon Man
Paleoanthropologist Qiang Ji, of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and colleagues tried to sequence ancient DNA from several samples of the Harbin skull’s bone and its one remaining tooth, but they had no luck. Proteins tend to be hardier molecules than DNA, though, and in samples from the skull’s temporal bone (the ones on the sides of the head, just behind the cheekbones), the researchers struck pay dirt.
They found fragments of a total of 95 proteins. Four of these had variations that were distinct to the Denisovan lineage, and the Harbin skull matched Denisovans on three of them. That’s enough to confidently say that the Harbin skull had belonged to a Denisovan. So for the past few years, we've had images of an almost uncannily well-preserved Denisovan skull—which is a pretty big deal, especially when you consider its complicated history.
While the world is now aware of it, until 2021, only one person had known what the skull looked like since its discovery in the 1930s. It was unearthed in Harbin, in northeast China, during the Japanese occupation of the area. Not wanting it to be seized by the occupying government, the person who found the skull immediately hid it, and he kept it hidden for most of the rest of his life.
He eventually turned it over to scientists in 2018,
who published
their analysis
in 2021
. That analysis placed the Harbin skull, along with a number of other fossils from China, in a distinct lineage within our genus,
Homo,
making them our species' closest fossil relatives. They called this alleged new species
Homo longi
, or "Dragon Man."
The decision to classify
Homo longi as
a new species was largely due to the skull's unique combination of features (which we'll discuss below). But it was a controversial decision, partly because paleoanthropologists don't entirely agree about whether we should even call
Neanderthals
a distinct species. If the line between Neanderthals and our species is that blurry, many in the field have questioned whether
Homo longi
could be considered a distinct species, when it's even closer to us than the Neanderthals.
Meanwhile, the 2021 paper also left room for debate on whether the skull might actually have belonged to a Denisovan rather than a distinct new species. Its authors acknowledge that one of the fossils they label as
Homo longi
had already been identified as a Denisovan based on its protein sequences. They also point out that the Harbin skull has rather large molars, which seem to be a common feature in Denisovans.
The paper's authors argued that their
Homo longi
should be a separate branch of the hominin lineage, more closely related to us than to Denisovans or Neanderthals. But if the Harbin skull looked so much like Denisovan fossils and so little like fossils from our species, the alleged relationship begins to look pretty dubious. In the end, the 2021 paper's authors dodged the issue by saying that "new genetic material will test the relationship of these populations to each other and to the Denisovans."
Which turned out to be exactly what happened.
A ghost lineage comes to life
Denisovans are the ghost in our family tree. For scientists, a “ghost lineage” is one that’s known mostly from genetic evidence, not fossils; like a ghost, it has a presence we can sense but no physical form we can touch. With the extremely well-preserved Harbin skull identified as a Denisovan, though, we’re finally able to look our “ghost” cousins in the face.
Paleogeneticists have recovered Denisovan DNA from tiny fragments of bone and teeth, and
even from the soil of a cave floor
. Genomics researchers have found segments of Denisovan DNA woven into the genomes of some modern humans, revealing just how close our two species once were. But the handful of Denisovan fossils paleoanthropologists have unearthed are mostly small fragments—a finger bone here, a tooth there, a jawbone someplace else—that don’t reveal much about how Denisovans lived or what they looked like.
We know they existed and that they were something slightly different from
Homo sapiens
or Neanderthals. We even know when and where they lived and a surprising amount about

data.title: Let's Talk About Writing in Tech
data.author: gmoniava
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了技术文档和教程在编程学习中的重要性，尽管它们被视为关键资源，但质量不佳的文档和教程常常让开发者更加困惑，从而阻碍学习。2017年GitHub的调查显示，“不完整或令人困惑的文档”是开源项目的主要问题。原因之一是开发者常忽视写作是一项独立技能，需要专门锻炼。即使擅长编码，也可能不善于书面表达。为改善这一状况，开发者应提升写作能力，组织则可通过收集用户反馈、聘请技术写作人员以及关注文档相关问题来改进文档质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术文档和开发人员沟通问题的本质及解决方案

不同观点：
• mdaniel：认为问题不在开发人员的技术能力，而在于缺少“初学者心态”或同理心。开发人员需要回想自己15分钟前还不知道答案时的状态，并据此调整产品设计以符合用户的心理模型。同时强调文档是与用户需求进行“同理心管理”的过程。

• jamesgill：基于技术写作经验指出，文档问题的核心不在写作技巧，而在于分析和理解受众的能力。他认为“写作”本身相对简单，关键在于设计出符合受众需求的文档内容。

• theletterf：赞同文档重要性，但认为原文讨论不充分，推荐了Chris Ward的技术写作书籍，并质疑开发团队是否了解技术写作职位的存在，建议聘请专业技术写作者。

• crosser：分享了其所在组织如何通过专门的文档写作团队促使开发人员自行编写文档的经验，指出若开发人员不写，技术写作者会介入，但会导致开发人员花费更多时间审核和修正。

• tolerance：对LLM（大型语言模型）在技术文档写作中的应用持怀疑态度，认为AI无法传递技术写作中特有的“氛围”和“指导性”，而这些是人们在学习过程中所重视的元素。

• x2tyfi：持相反观点，认为LLM在技术文档写作中有巨大潜力，并举例说明工程师通过LLM生成的文档质量远高于以往的手工写作，尤其在结构固定的文档类型中效果更佳。

• scrubs：强调技术文档和沟通任务不应交给不擅长沟通的技术人员，建议对工程师进行定期培训，并明确区分销售、营销和工程沟通的不同。同时批评了技术文档中的“日记式”写作和过度使用术语的问题，主张简洁有效的沟通。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于LLM是否能有效帮助技术文档写作。tolerance认为AI缺乏“氛围”，而x2tyfi则认为LLM在某些结构化文档中表现出色。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是技术文档写作中“同理心”和管理受众假设的重要性，mdaniel和jamesgill都提到了这一点。
- 对技术写作职位的认知和需求存在分歧，theletterf强调专业技术写作者角色的重要性，而crosser则通过实例说明开发人员自行编写文档的必要性。

44349223.article_content:
Let’s Talk About Writing in Tech
Jun 18, 2025
software-development
The Problem
2024 Stack Overflow
survey
listed
technical documentation
and
written tutorials
as two of the top three resources for learning to code.
Despite this I’m sure you’ve experienced (likely more than once) that
frustrating moment when you finish reading a tutorial or documentation
and feel even more confused than when you started.
This can be a serious problem because poor documentation and tutorials can
discourage developers from learning or adopting a certain technology.
Evidence
Actually in 2017, GitHub's Open Source
Survey
showed "incomplete
or confusing documentation" to be the top pain point. I doubt the
situation has significantly changed since then, at least judging from my
personal experience and experience of others with whom I have
interacted.
Possible Causes and Solutions
One possible cause, in my opinion, is that we as developers need to
realize that writing is a
separate skill
and it needs to be worked on to
be improved.
You can be an excellent coder but still struggle to explain your ideas
clearly in writing. So if we, as developers, work a bit on this skill,
maybe we can improve the situation a little bit.
For example in academia, it's well understood that being an expert in a
subject doesn't automatically make someone a good teacher. The same
principle applies here.
Organizations can also help improve the situation by:
regularly gathering feedback from developers who use the organization's documentation and making improvements accordingly.
adding technical writers to support documentation efforts.
paying more attention to documentation related issues on GitHub repositories, which, in my experience, are sometimes overlooked.

data.title: Triaging security issues reported by third parties
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站为防止AI公司大规模爬取数据导致的服务器过载问题，采用了名为Anubis的防护系统。Anubis基于Hashcash的证明工作量（Proof-of-Work）机制，要求访问者完成一定计算任务，以增加大规模爬取的成本。虽然对普通用户影响不大，但对大量爬取行为会显著增加负担。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的指纹识别技术争取时间，最终目标是更精准地识别真实用户与自动化爬虫。同时，使用Anubis需要启用现代JavaScript功能，某些插件如JShelter可能会干扰其运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件安全与维护责任

不同观点：
• **runningmike 的观点**：OpenSSF Scorecards 的一些测试标准不合理，尤其是对于那些不使用 GitHub Actions 或者只有一个开发者的项目来说。他认为这些标准过于排外，并不真正开放，不适合小型项目或个人项目。

• **tptacek 的观点**：同意 unpaid volunteers 不应该感到必须在截止日期前修复安全漏洞的压力，特别是在开源项目中。同时指出，评论中提到的 GPZ 相关的漏洞是非常严重的，虽然对开源项目维护者的压力表示理解，但像 Google 这样的大公司可能会最终介入修复这些漏洞。

补充讨论：
• **cwillu 的观点**：提到“Proof of work captcha”似乎已经失效，暗示在漏洞报告或安全测试中可能存在自动化工具滥用的问题，进一步增加了开源项目维护者的负担。

争议焦点：
• 开源项目维护者是否应该承担修复安全漏洞的责任，特别是当他们是非付费志愿者时。
• OpenSSF Scorecards 的测试标准是否适用于所有项目，尤其是小型或个人项目。
• 如何在确保安全的前提下，减轻开源项目维护者的压力，避免他们被大量无效或低质量的漏洞报告淹没。

这些观点共同反映了开源社区在安全维护和项目可持续性方面面临的挑战，特别是如何平衡项目维护者的责任与社区贡献者的参与。

44315443.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.
44315443.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站为防止AI公司大规模爬取数据导致的服务器过载问题，采用了名为Anubis的防护系统。Anubis基于Hashcash的证明工作量（Proof-of-Work）机制，要求访问者完成一定计算任务，以增加大规模爬取的成本。虽然对普通用户影响不大，但对大量爬取行为会显著增加负担。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的指纹识别技术争取时间，最终目标是更精准地识别真实用户与自动化爬虫。同时，使用Anubis需要启用现代JavaScript功能，某些插件如JShelter可能会干扰其运行。

• **tptacek 的观点**：同意 unpaid volunteers 不应该感到必须在截止日期前修复安全漏洞的压力，特别是在开源项目中。同时指出，评论中提到的 GPZ 相关的漏洞是非常严重的，虽然对开源项目维护者的压力表示理解，但像 Google 这样的大公司可能会最终介入修复这些漏洞。

补充讨论：

争议焦点：
• 开源项目维护者是否应该承担修复安全漏洞的责任，特别是当他们是非付费志愿者时。
• OpenSSF Scorecards 的测试标准是否适用于所有项目，尤其是小型或个人项目。
• 如何在确保安全的前提下，减轻开源项目维护者的压力，避免他们被大量无效或低质量的漏洞报告淹没。

这些观点共同反映了开源社区在安全维护和项目可持续性方面面临的挑战，特别是如何平衡项目维护者的责任与社区贡献者的参与。

data.title: Airpass – Easily overcome WiFi time limits
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: Airpass for Mac 是一款可以更改设备 MAC 地址的工具。WiFi 网络会记录设备的 MAC 地址，即使使用不同凭证登录，仍可能阻止设备连接。通过更改 MAC 地址，Airpass 让网络误以为这是新设备，从而避免连接限制。该工具由 Tiago Alves 在旅途中开发。

主要讨论点：通过改变MAC地址以实现不同目的的技术方法及道德与合法性问题

不同观点：
• classichasclass和purplehat_提供了在不同操作系统（macOS和Linux）上手动更改MAC地址的具体命令和脚本。classichasclass的方案涉及使用`airport`和`ifconfig`命令，而purplehat_提供了一个适用于Debian的脚本，并指出`openssl rand`命令可能生成无效MAC地址。
• ammar2讨论了现代操作系统内置的MAC地址随机化功能，提到了macOS、Android和Windows中相关设置的位置，并提供了官方文档链接。

• kazinator指出Android系统中MAC地址随机化是一个基本隐私功能，并提到设备指纹识别的问题。

44310763.article_content:
Download Airpass for Mac
Why?
Wifi networks collect a reference to your computer (called MAC address) when you login. That way, when you try to login again, even with different credentials, they detect that it is the same device and do not allow you to continue using it.
How?
By renewing your device's MAC address, the wifi network will not identify your computer and therefore is tricked into thinking it's a new device. When you try to login again it won't trigger the error message and you're free to use it.
Made while ✈️ by
Tiago Alves

data.title: Phoenix.new – Remote AI Runtime for Phoenix
data.author: wut42
data.article_summary: Chris McCord，Elixir的Phoenix框架的创建者，介绍了其最新项目Phoenix.new。这是一个全在线编码代理，专为Elixir和Phoenix设计，运行在浏览器中，利用Fly.io的虚拟机技术，提供完整的shell访问，无需担心本地环境。Phoenix.new允许代理安装软件包、运行程序，并实时测试和部署应用。它使用无头浏览器与应用程序交互，能自动检查前端更改和日志。通过与GitHub集成和预置的gh CLI，它可以处理代码库和内部项目。该工具旨在简化协作和实时应用程序的开发，使应用程序从创建之初就生活在云端，并具备可分享的URL和自动错误检测功能。Phoenix.new为开发者提供了强大的自动化编码能力，减少了繁琐的手动工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Phoenix和Fly.io结合的开发工具及其引发的讨论

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
  - colecut表示，作为一个PHP开发者，通过Fly.io和Phoenix的结合，他能够在不到45分钟内部署一个多房间的Tic Tac Toe游戏，尽管他对Elixir和Phoenix了解不多，但工具的简便性让他印象深刻。
  - arrowsmith对LLM在Elixir开发中的应用感到兴奋，认为这样的工具能弥补Elixir相对于Python和JS的不足。

• 技术细节与功能询问：
  - chrismccord（Phoenix创建者）指出phoenix.new是一个全球Elixir集群，并表示愿意回答其他技术问题。
  - losvedir对AI如何管理上下文和模型选择提出疑问，特别是关于Gemini模型和Claude Code的使用。
  - liampulles关心是否会被绑定到Fly.io平台，并希望能在其他平台上开发。

• 负面反馈与使用体验：
  - itsautomatisch表示快速消耗了信用额度，且UI问题和文档不足让他对Fly.io感到失望。
  - jsmo和rustc对$20/月的服务包含哪些具体内容感到困惑。

• 对工具的哲学与社会影响反思：
  - travisgriggs对“这是否是未来”持矛盾态度，认为这种工具虽然能减轻一些开发负担，但也反映出编程的复杂性。
  - krainboltgreene对社区领导者专注于可能反工人的工具建设感到不满。

• 对Rails开发者的吸引力：
  - poisonta认为Phoenix需要一个类似ActiveRecord的数据库抽象层，以吸引更多Rails开发者。

  - psadri认为利用AI构建过渡性应用是一个进步，但同时也提出如果AI能写应用代码，那么应用本身是否会消失的问题。

- 多个评论提到对Fly.io的定价和信用使用情况的透明度需求。

44328326.article_content:
Author
Name
Chris McCord
@chris_mccord
@chris_mccord
Iâm Chris McCord, the creator of Elixirâs Phoenix framework. For the past several months, Iâve been working on a skunkworks project at Fly.io, and itâs time to show it off.
I wanted LLM agents to work just as well with Elixir as they do with Python and JavaScript. Last December, in order to figure out what that was going to take, I started a little weekend project to find out how difficult it would be to build a coding agent in Elixir.
A few weeks later, I had it spitting out working Phoenix applications and driving a full in-browser IDE. I knew this wasn’t going to stay a weekend project.
If you follow me on Twitter, you’ve probably seen me teasing this work as it picked up steam. We’re at a point where we’re pretty serious about this thing, and so it’s time to make a formal introduction.
World, meet
Phoenix.new
, a batteries-included fully-online coding agent tailored to Elixir and Phoenix. I think it’s going to be the fastest way to build collaborative, real-time applications.
Let’s see it in action:
What’s Interesting About Phoenix.new
First, even though it runs entirely in your browser, Phoenix.new gives both you and your agent a root shell, in an ephemeral virtual machine (a
Fly Machine
) that gives our agent loop free rein to install things and run programs  â without any risk of messing up your local machine. You don’t think about any of this; you just open up the VSCode interface, push the shell button, and there you are, on the isolated machine you share with the Phoenix.new agent.
Second, it’s an agent system I built specifically for Phoenix. Phoenix is about real-time collaborative applications, and Phoenix.new knows what that means. To that end, Phoenix.new includes, in both its UI and its agent tools, a full browser. The Phoenix.new agent uses that browser “headlessly” to check its own front-end changes and interact with the app. Because it’s a full browser, instead of trying to iterate on screenshots, the agent sees real page content and JavaScript state â with or without a human present.
What Root Access Gets Us
Agents build software the way you did when you first got started, the way you still do today when you prototype things. They don’t carefully design Docker container layers and they don’t really do release cycles. An agent wants to pop a shell and get its fingernails dirty.
A fully isolated virtual machine means Phoenix.new’s fingernails can get
arbitrarily dirty.
If it wants to add a package to
mix.exs
, it can do that and then run
mix phx.server
or
mix test
and check the output. Sure. Every agent can do that. But if it wants to add an APT package to the base operating system, it can do that too, and make sure it worked. It owns the whole environment.
This offloads a huge amount of tedious, repetitive work.
At his
AI Startup School talk last week
, Andrej Karpathy related his experience of building a restaurant menu visualizer, which takes camera pictures of text menus and transforms all the menu items into pictures. The code, which he vibe-coded with an LLM agent, was the easy part; he had it working in an afternoon. But getting the app online took him a whole week.
With Phoenix.new, I’m taking dead aim at this problem. The apps we produce live in the cloud from the minute they launch. They have private, shareable URLs (we detect anything the agent generates with a bound port and give it a preview URL underneath
phx.run
, with integrated port-forwarding), they integrate with Github, and they inherit all the infrastructure guardrails of Fly.io: hardware virtualization, WireGuard, and isolated networks.
Githubâs
gh
CLI is installed by default. So the agent knows how to clone any repo, or browse issues, and you can even authorize it for internal repositories to get it working with your teamâs existing projects and dependencies.
Full control of the environment also closes the loop between the agent and deployment. When Phoenix.new boots an app, it watches the logs, and tests the application. When an action triggers an error, Phoenix.new notices and gets to work.
Watch It Build In Real Time
Phoenix.new
can interact with web applications the way users do: with a real browser.
The Phoenix.new environment includes a headless Chrome browser that our agent knows how to drive. Prompt it to add a front-end feature to your application, and it won’t just sketch the code out and make sure it compiles and lints. It’ll pull the app up itself and poke at the UI, simultaneously looking at the page content, JavaScript state, and server-side logs.
Phoenix is all about
“live” real-time
interactivity, and gives us seamless live reload. The user interface for Phoenix.new itself includes a live preview of the app being worked on, so you can kick back and watch it build front-end features incrementally. Any other
.phx.run
tabs you have open also update as it goes. It’s wild.

data.title: Writing 23 Games in 24 Days (in Rust)
data.author: ostwilkens
data.article_summary:
本文记录了作者在24天内使用Rust和Bevy引擎开发23款小游戏的挑战。这些游戏大多简单且具有互动性，部分游戏使用了Stable Diffusion生成图像，并可通过浏览器游玩。以下是部分游戏的简述：

1. **7月16日**：基本rogue-lite游戏，受Vampire Survivors启发。
2. **7月17日**：横向卷轴射击游戏，使用LLM生成物品名称和属性，Stable Diffusion生成图像。
3. **7月18日**：反应速度测试游戏。
4. **7月19日**：调用外部API展示数据。
5. **7月20日**：打地鼠游戏的变种，使用 otter 形象。
6. **7月21日**：第一人称视角测试，名为"Immortal Demons"。
7. **7月22日**：测试Bevy的bloom功能。
8. **7月23日**：第三人称竞速游戏，支持键盘和触屏输入。
9. **7月24日**：记忆游戏，使用Blender、Figma和Midjourney制作3D图形。
10. **7月25日**：基于轮子物理的平台游戏。

挑战期间有几天因旅行暂停，后续几天继续迭代和优化之前的游戏，加入新功能如动态音乐、脚步声和冲刺。最后，作者提到了一些额外项目，如基本rogue-lite和支持多人模式的FPS游戏。

所有游戏可在作者GitHub页面访问并试玩。

7. **7月22日**：测试Bevy的bloom功能。

挑战期间有几天因旅行暂停，后续几天继续迭代和优化之前的游戏，加入新功能如动态音乐、脚步声和冲刺。最后，作者提到了一些额外项目，如基本rogue-lite和支持多人模式的FPS游戏。

data.title: Using Microsoft's New CLI Text Editor on Ubuntu
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: Microsoft推出了开源命令行文本编辑器**Edit**，旨在为Windows用户提供一个易用的CLI文本编辑器，因为Windows缺乏内置的CLI编辑器。Edit是基于Rust开发的，具有现代界面和类似VS Code的输入控制，目标是简单和快速。它具备一些基本功能，如查找替换、字宽调整、多文件编辑等，但缺少语法高亮和配色方案等高级功能。虽然Edit主要面向Windows用户，但也可以在Linux和macOS上使用，并且由于其与VS Code相似的快捷键设置，可能会吸引一些Linux用户。目前，Edit没有官方Linux安装包，但可以通过下载二进制文件或Snap构建来运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对经典文本编辑器及其相关技术概念的讨论，包括历史背景、技术区别、跨平台使用以及编辑器的设计与功能。

不同观点：
• [felineflock] 认为文章混淆了TUI和CLI等不同概念，并指出新编辑器实际上是1991年MS-DOS 5中EDIT程序的重新实现。他还提到在VIM流行之前，vi是主流编辑器，并列举了Windows上曾存在的其他编辑器选项。
• [simonw] 分享了在macOS上通过Docker运行Edit的步骤，并提供了相关指南链接，强调了该编辑器的跨平台可用性。
• [hiAndrewQuinn] 讨论了终端中快捷键的使用，特别是Ctrl组合键的功能，认为这些快捷键应该更广为人知。
• [orsenthil] 赞赏该编辑器的易用性和直观性，并批评Linux中主流编辑器（如nano、vim、emacs）对新手不够友好，认为可以借鉴该编辑器的设计。
• [seabrookmx] 认为该编辑器功能过于简陋，缺乏语法高亮等现代编辑器常见功能，推荐了另一个TUI编辑器micro。
• [czarit] 对该项目在Rust中不使用现有成熟库（如termios）而自行实现所有功能表示困惑，认为这种做法在Rust社区中很不寻常。
• [jll29] 分享了为实现“DOS兼容性”而添加的别名设置建议。
• [aa-jv] 提出是否有人考虑过将PC-Write编辑器移植到Linux，并回忆了其在80年代的使用体验。
• [posix86] 希望Windows终端能被移植到Linux，因为其在处理Ctrl+C的多功能性上表现出色。
• [jmmv] 提到了自己曾写过一篇关于DOS和Windows编辑器历史的文章，并提供了链接。
• [VagabundoP] 对没有标准化的剪切、复制、粘贴键表示疑惑，认为这导致了不必要的效率损失。
• [neoden] 询问了编辑器截图中使用的字体。
• [declan_roberts] 表达了对该编辑器UI设计的喜爱，认为其设计让他怀念Windows 3.0和DOS时代。
• [__MatrixMan__] 批评微软的命名策略，认为其与“meta”和“X”一样令人困惑，并暗示这种趋势可能导致不良后果。
• [culebron21] 提到Norton Commander及其编辑器，认为其是DOS时代方便的文件编辑工具，并指出了其现代继任者如Midnight Commander和FAR Manager，同时讨论了这些工具在使用中的小问题。

补充讨论：
• 该讨论中多次提到了不同编辑器的历史背景和技术特点，特别是对新手友好性的讨论。
• 跨平台使用和编辑器功能扩展（如快捷键、语法高亮）也是讨论的重点。
• 对微软命名策略的批评和DOS时代编辑器的怀旧构成了另一条讨论线。
• 技术实现上的选择（如Rust项目中的自行实现）也是争议的焦点之一。

44306892.article_content:
If you spend a lot time in a terminal on Linux you’ll have preferred command-line text editor, but Microsoft’s recently announced open-source offering, simply called
Edit
, might be worth checking out — if only so you know you’re not missing out.
Edit
is a remake/reboot of the old
MS-DOS Editor
, updated to suit current sensibilities. Built using Rust, it aims to deliver a user experience that, per its GitHub page, provides
“modern interface and input controls similar to VS Code.”
Microsoft says it made
Edit
“to provide an accessible editor that even users largely unfamiliar with terminals can easily use”
on Windows if/when needed, out-of-the-box (as recent versions of Windows do not include a CLI text editor in recent versions).
The arrival of
Edit
will mean Windows devs aren’t forced to fire up notepad.exe to make a simple shell script edit, but is there any benefit to running the app on Linux?
Note:
When I spotlight apps, tools and utilities on this blog, it’s
not
because I think you (or anyone) “MUST” use them. I simply showcase choices. Whether you choose to use them is up to you.
Why would Linux users use
Edit
?
As straightforward to use as it seems
Windows is the primary target for
Edit
since it lacks a built-in CLI text editor natively so the fact you can use
Edit
on Linux (and macOS) is more of bonus than purpose.
But if you use Linux and
VSCode
your muscle memory might like the fact
Edit
shares many of the latter’s keybindings. This could make it easier to slot in to your workflow compared to
vim
or
nano
(though I stress it’s not a replacement for either of those).
Not that only avowed VSCode fans will see the appeal.
The simplicity of the text-driven UI (TUI) makes it less complex to learn, while the speed of
Edit
, even when seeking across lines in giant 1GB+ files, is impressive — both USPs are by design.
Working with multiple files is easy enough too
Eager to avoid “how to exit vim” memes, Microsoft designed
Edit
as a modeless text editor (as opposed to a multi-mode one like Vim, where you need to learn how to activate different modes and switch between them as needed).
You can
use a mouse or a keyboard
to access menus, select lines or regions of text, position the caret, etc which makes using it feel more intuitive in use than the either/or approach of (admittedly more capable) alternatives.
Edit
offers up a modest, lightweight set of features (and an equally modest footprint: a mere 250kB out of the box, and fast file opening) including:
Find and Replace
(supports
Match Case
&
Regular Expression
)
Word wrap
on resize
(optional)
Set tab/space indentation
Set/change file encoding
Line Feed (LF) or Carriage Return + Line Feed ( CRLF)
Open multiple files
There’s pretty much all there is right now.
Edit
has no syntax highlighting, no range of colour schemes, no command prompt, and few creature comforts common in other command line text editors.
Edit
is designed to edit text, rather than handle complex task better suited to IDEs.
More features are planned, including colour schemes and a settings TUI, so the list of features will grow in time, but as Microsoft’s aim is speed and simplicity, don’t expect too many bells and whistles.
Edit
is open source so anyone can modify, contribute, package or fork it.
How to Run
Edit
on Ubuntu
Edit
is free, open source software that works on Windows, Linux and macOS (so no, you don’t need to using Windows to make use of it).
Right now there is no official “installer” for Linux, and no unofficial DEB of PPA, though
there is a snap
. A couple of Linux distributions now package
Edit
, including Arch Linux, and Manjaro, so if you use one of those, you can install it properly.
To run
Edit
on Ubuntu you can download the latest binary from the
project GitHub releases page
(be sure to select the correct one for your architecture), extract the package,
cd
into the extracted folder, then launch the binary each time you want to use it:
Download the latest release
(link above)
Extract the archive
(right-click in
Nautilus
>
Extract
)
Open a terminal app
(such as the new
Pytxis
in Ubuntu 25.10
)
Navigate to the extracted folder:
cd /path/to/
Run
Edit
directly:
./edit
To install the unofficial snap build use
App Center
(search ‘msedit’) or run
sudo snap install msedit
from the command line, and use
msedit
to launch it. On my laptop, the snap takes ~5 seconds to open. The official binary is instantaneous. YMMV.
From there, the interface is easy enough to figure out.
Give it a try and let me know what you think!
CLI Tools
Edit
Microsoft
Text Editor

data.title: My First Impressions of Gleam
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文作者正在学习Gleam编程语言，并选择通过解析旧的AIM聊天日志来实践。Gleam是一种类似于Elixir且支持静态类型的语言。作者首先解决了如何解析命令行参数的问题，发现Gleam标准库中没有相关模块，但通过第三方库`argv`实现了简单的命令行参数读取。接着，作者尝试使用`gleam build`命令来编译项目，但发现生成的BEAM字节码无法直接执行，且文档不够清晰。最终，作者着手实现了一个简单的日志解析函数，从纯文本日志中提取聊天信息。作者计划逐步处理更复杂的日志格式并添加web前端。通过这个项目，作者正在探索Gleam的功能以及其在解析任务中的应用。

44348442.article_content:
I’m
looking for a new programming language
to learn this year, and
Gleam
looks like the most fun. It’s an Elixir-like language that supports static typing.
I read the
language tour
, and it made sense to me, but I need to build something before I can judge a programming language well.
I’m sharing some notes on my first few hours using Gleam in case they’re helpful to others learning Gleam or to the team developing the language.
My project: Parsing old AIM logs
🔗︎
I used AOL Instant Messenger from about 1999 to 2007. For most of that time, I used AIM clients that logged my conversations, but they varied in formats. Most of the log formats are XML or HTML, which make re-reading those logs a pain.
The simplest AIM logs are the plaintext logs, which look like this:
Session Start (DumbAIMScreenName:Jane): Mon Sep 12 18:44:17 2005
[18:44] Jane: hi
[18:55] Me: hey whats up
Session Close (Jane): Mon Sep 12 18:56:02 2005
Every decade or so, I try writing a universal AIM log parser to get all of my old logs into a consistent, readable format. Unfortunately, I always get bored and give up partway through. My last attempt was
seven years ago
, when I tried doing it in Python 2.7.
Parsing logs is a great match for Gleam because some parts of the project are easy (e.g., parsing the plaintext logs), so I can do the easy parts while I get the hang of Gleam as a language and gradually build up to the harder log formats and adding a web frontend.
I’ve also heard that functional languages lend themselves especially well to parsing tasks, and I’ve never understood why, so it’s a good opportunity to learn.
My background in programming languages
🔗︎
I’ve been a programmer for 20 years, but I’m no language design connoisseur. I’m sharing things about Gleam I find unintuitive or difficult to work with, but they’re not language critiques, just candid reactions.
I’ve never worked in a langauge that’s designed for functional programming. The closest would be JavaScript. The
languages I know best
are Go and Python.
How do I parse command-line args?
🔗︎
The first thing I wanted to do was figure out how to parse a command-line argument so I could call my app like this:
./log-parser ~/logs/aim/plaintext
But there’s no Gleam standard library module for reading command-line arguments. I found
glint
, and it felt super complicated for just reading one command-line argument. Then, I realized there’s a simpler third-party library called
argv
.
I can parse the command-line argument like this:
pub
fn
main
()
{
case
argv.
load
().arguments
{
[path]
->
io.
println
(
"command-line arg is "
<>
path)
_
->
io.
println
(
"Usage: gleam run <directory_path>"
)
}
}
$ gleam run ~/whatever
Compiled in 0.01s
Running log_parser.main
command-line arg is /home/mike/whatever
Cool, easy enough!
What does
gleam build
do?
🔗︎
I got my program to run with
gleam run
, but I was curious if I could compile an executable like
go build
or
zig build
does.
$ gleam build
Compiled in 0.01s
Hmm, compiled what? I couldn’t see a binary anywhere.
The
documentation for
gleam build
just says “Build the project” but doesn’t explain
what
it builds or where it stores the build artifact.
There’s a
build
directory, but it doesn’t produce an obvious executable.
$ rm -rf build && gleam build
Downloading packages
Downloaded
5
packages in 0.00s
Compiling argv
Compiling gleam_stdlib
Compiling filepath
Compiling gleeunit
Compiling simplifile
Compiling log_parser
Compiled in 0.52s
$ ls -1 build/
dev
gleam-dev-erlang.lock
gleam-dev-javascript.lock
gleam-lsp-erlang.lock
gleam-lsp-javascript.lock
gleam-prod-erlang.lock
gleam-prod-javascript.lock
packages
From poking around, I think the executables are under
build/dev/erlang/log_parser/ebin/
:
$ ls -1 build/dev/erlang/log_parser/ebin/
log_parser.app
log_parser.beam

data.title: Captain Cook's missing ship found after sinking 250 years ago
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 文章报道了詹姆斯·库克船长的船只“奋进号”（HMS Endeavour）的残骸在美国罗德岛新港港湾被发现。这艘船在1768至1771年间成为首艘到达澳大利亚东部的欧洲船只，后在1778年美国独立战争期间被故意沉没作为封锁。经过25年的研究，澳大利亚国家海事博物馆确认残骸为“奋进号”，尽管之前有其他机构批评其结论“过于仓促”。考古学家通过木材和船体结构的比对，确定其与“奋进号”几乎完全吻合，尽管未发现能立即确认身份的文物。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于HMS Endeavour（也称Lord Sandwich）的历史、重新命名及其相关新闻报道的讨论

不同观点：
• cromulent认为，关于HMS Endeavour的宣布早在三年前就已经做出，质疑为何现在才重新提起。他引用了一篇2022年的新闻链接来支持自己的观点。
• duxup承认重新命名的合理性，但对从“HMS Endeavour”这样一个富有历史意义的名字改为“Lord Sandwich”表示不解，认为后者在现代听起来像是一个论坛用户名，缺乏庄重感。
• CoastalCoder关注的是沉船的具体位置，并提到Narraganset Bay最近的船只活动，怀疑这些活动是否与HMS Endeavour的沉船有关。
• BurningFrog对在独立报网站上看到Al Jazeera的视频感到奇怪，质疑这种媒体合作。
• HeyLaughingBoy对Lord Sandwich作为历史性船只最终被故意沉没的命运表示遗憾，认为这种结局对于一艘创造过历史的船只来说是可悲的。

补充讨论：
• anonymous344抱怨网站对手机用户不友好，虽然这一评论与主要讨论点关系不大，但指出了网站用户体验的问题。
• freedomben用幽默的方式表达了自己的误解，提到自己父母的大脑误将“Captain Cook”读成了“Captain Hook”，并对这一错误感到失望，增添了一些轻松的氛围。
• mediumsmart用双关语评论“你不应该烹饪一个三明治”，虽然与历史讨论无关，但展示了语言游戏的幽默。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于对“HMS Endeavour”改名为“Lord Sandwich”的合理性和名称适应现代语境的讨论。一部分人认为新名称缺乏历史感和庄重性。

The remains of captain
Cook
’s ship,
HMS Endeavour
,
has been located
off the US coast after sinking 250 years ago.
Between 1768 and 1771, the ship became the first European
vessel
to reach eastern Australia. It was then sold and renamed the Lord
Sandwich
before sinking off the US coast
during the American War of Independence in 1778.
For
centuries the ship was lost
, but now the wreck has been found in Newport Harbour,
Rhode Island
.
The finding was announced in a
new report
by the Australian National Maritime Museum (ANMM) and experts have identified the wreck as RI 2394.
Daryl Karp, Museum director explained the findings in the report are the result of 25 years of archaeological research and underwater investigations.
open image in gallery
Edward Fage, [Newport and its environs, ca. 1778], William L. Clements Library, University of Michigan, 8380. Note ‘Sunken Ships’ indicated due west of North Battery (circled)
(
Australian National Maritime Museum
)
The shipwreck was compared to historic plans for Cook’s ship revealing measurements aligned with those taken of a 1768 survey.
Kieran Hosty, ANMM archaeologist, who co-wrote the report, said: “The timbers are British timbers. The size of all the timber scantlings are almost identical to
Endeavour
, and I’m talking within millimetres - not inches, but millimetres.
“The stem scarf is identical, absolutely identical. This stem scarf is also a very unique feature - we’ve gone through a whole bunch of 18th-century ship’s plans, and we can’t find anything else like it.”
The ship was used for British troop transport and a prison ship in the American War of Independence. In this time, it was renamed Lord Sandwich.
When American and French besieged Newport Harbour the ship was one of 13 vessels deliberately sunk to act as a submerged blockage. It was never salvaged and remained sank.
open image in gallery
Mosaic showing frame and scuttling hole beneath letter board, north is at bottom of image (John D. Broadwater)
(
Australian National Maritime Museum
)
Archaeologist James Hunter, co-author of the report, explained that it was unlikely they would find artefacts that would provide an immediate identification. Anything that was of value would have been taken out of the ship before it sank.
However, everything experts have found so far is indicative of the 18th century.
The finding comes after a preliminary report in 2022, identified the same wreck as the
HMS Endeavour
. But it was met with criticism by the museum’s research partners, the Rhode Island Marine Archaeology Project (RIMAP) who said the finding was “premature” and a “breach of contract”, claiming that it was the lead organisation for the study, The Telegraph reported.
In a statement, ANMM said it was not ruling out other candidate shipwreck sites.

data.title: Show HN: Nxtscape – an open-source agentic browser
data.author: felarof
data.article_summary: Nxtscape是一款开源的代理浏览器，注重隐私保护和本地AI功能。它允许用户在本地运行AI代理，而不是依赖云端，从而确保浏览数据不会外泄。Nxtscape基于Chromium，界面和操作类似于Google Chrome，支持Chrome扩展。用户可以自行选择AI提供商（如OpenAI、Anthropic）或使用本地模型Ollama。其目标是通过AI自动化提升用户效率，同时保障数据安全。与Chrome、Brave、Arc、Dia、Perplexity Comet等浏览器相比，Nxtscape更加注重隐私和开放源代码。用户可以参与贡献，帮助改进浏览器功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于具备代理功能的浏览器（agentic browser）的可行性、安全性、实现方式及市场前景的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持与期待**：
   - [kevinsync] 认为这种浏览器可以成为个人助理，帮助自动化处理各种任务，如过滤广告、垃圾信息、自动化操作等，非常有价值，尤其在处理大量书签和减少干扰方面。
   - [wanderingmind] 提出具体使用场景，如从网站提取数据文件，认为如果能实现自动化将非常有用。
   - [varenc] 尝试了该浏览器的一些功能，虽然遇到一些问题，但整体体验积极，期待后续改进。

• **对安全性与技术实现的担忧**：
   - [mullingitover] 认为这种浏览器有巨大的安全风险，尤其是涉及到敏感账户和不受信任的网络输入时，可能会导致严重的安全漏洞。
   - [arjunchint] 指出通过Chrome扩展也能实现类似的功能，且浏览器作为安全风险高的载体，需要专门的团队持续更新安全补丁。

• **对产品概念与市场的质疑**：
   - [hannob] 对“agentic browser”的概念表示困惑，质疑其是否为一个常见和明确的术语。
   - [gtsop] 建议使用现有的 robust 扩展，而不是开发新浏览器，认为这是更合理的实现方式。
   - [ppqqrr] 认为目前的关键在于提升整个Web体验，而不是专注于特定的浏览器应用。
   - [dvt] 强烈批评该概念，认为只是简单地将LLM叠加到Chrome上，缺乏技术创新，且聊天界面不适合生产力工具。
   - [deepdarkforest] 指出浏览器项目规模巨大，小团队难以成功，且面临Google等大公司的竞争，成功的可能性低。

• **其他具体问题**：
   - [admiralrohan] 关心项目的盈利模式和所使用的LLM及硬件要求。
   - [blindriver] 提到商标侵权问题，认为“nxtscape”与“Netscape”过于相似。

补充讨论：
- **产品定义不清**：部分评论者对“agentic browser”的定义感到困惑，认为需要更清晰的解释和定义。
- **技术实现路径的分歧**：一些评论者认为通过扩展而非全新浏览器可以实现类似功能，且更具可行性。
- **市场竞争与前景**：有评论者指出该领域竞争激烈，尤其是面对Google等大公司，小团队成功的难度大。
- **具体功能问题**：一些用户提到在使用过程中遇到的功能性问题，如tab组管理不当等。

Nxtscape Browser
Your browser, with AI superpowers 🚀
🌐 Nxtscape is an open-source agentic browser that runs AI agents locally. Your privacy-first alternative to Arc, Dia, and Perplexity Comet.
🔒 Privacy first - use your own API keys or run local models with Ollama. Your data stays on your computer.
💡 Join our
Discord
and help us build! Have feature requests?
Suggest anonymously here
.
Quick start
Download and install Nxtscape
Import your Chrome data (optional)
Connect your AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or local Ollama)
Start automating!
What makes Nxtscape special
Features
🏠 Feels like home - same familiar interface as Google Chrome, works with all your extensions
🤖 AI agents that run on YOUR browser, not in the cloud
🔒 Privacy first - bring your own keys or use local models with Ollama. Your browsing history stays on your computer
🚀 Open source and community driven - see exactly what's happening under the hood
🤝 (coming soon) MCP store to one-click install popular MCPs and use them directly in the browser bar
🛡️ (coming soon) Built-in AI ad blocker that works across more scenarios!
Demos
🤖 AI Agents in Action (
watch video
)
💬 Local AI Chat (
watch video
)
⚡ Productivity Tools (
watch video
)
Why we're building this
For the first time since Netscape in 1994, it feels like we can reimagine browsers from scratch. We saw how Cursor gave developers a 10x productivity boost, yet browsers feel stuck in the past.
You probably have 70+ tabs open right now. You're constantly fighting your browser instead of it helping you. Simple tasks like "order Tide Pods from my Amazon order history" should just work with AI agents.
We believe AI agents should automate your work locally and securely, not send your data to some search or ad company.
How we compare
vs Chrome
While we're grateful for Google open-sourcing Chromium, but Chrome hasn't evolved much in 10 years. No AI features, no automation, no MCP support.
vs Brave
We love what Brave started, but they've spread themselves too thin with crypto, search, VPNs. We're laser-focused on AI-powered browsing.
vs Arc/Dia
Many loved Arc, but it was closed source. When they abandoned users, there was no recourse. We're 100% open source - fork it anytime!
vs Perplexity Comet
They're a search/ad company. Your browser history becomes their product. We keep everything local.
Contributing
We'd love your help making Nxtscape better!

data.title: Hawaii Highways
data.author: yakattak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由Oscar Voss创建的非官方、非商业性网站，旨在为夏威夷的“道路学者”和游客提供有关夏威夷公路系统的信息。网站包括各岛屿的州际公路和州县公路的详细信息，如路线编号、名称、终点、里程等，并提供了一些历史资料和照片链接。网站还设有欧胡岛高速公路出口指南和一般信息页面，包括常见问题解答和旅游贴士。作者欢迎读者提供帮助以更新和改进网站内容，并提醒用户参考夏威夷交通部获取最新的路况信息。网站无广告，信息准确性不保证，建议在陌生地区行车前进行本地咨询。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [nrclark] 认为夏威夷作为一个群岛却拥有州际公路（interstates）具有一定的讽刺意味，同时指出夏威夷应获得与其他州相同的道路资金支持。他还提到对命名惯例或新兴特性的一些思考。

• [bob_theslob646] 对网站的创建表示钦佩，同时分享了在夏威夷大岛夜间驾驶的恐怖经历，强调了夜间驾驶的困难与危险性，特别是从Kona机场向南行驶的单车道、多弯道的路段。

44350978.article_content:
Hawaii Highways
An unofficial, non-commercial Internet guide to Hawaii's highways, for "roads scholars" and road users
Version 2.5, by
Oscar Voss
(based on
C.C. Slater
's original sites)
Limited updates since 2010
(See
What's new
for latest changes, including several updates since 2010, and planned major updates and other improvements)
Route lists
Aloha!
This site has lots of information on Hawaii's highway system, for "roads scholars" (a/k/a "roadgeeks"), and for tourists and others to plan their travels in the islands.
Click the dark green buttons on the left for lists of the Interstate, state, and some county highways on
the Big Island
(Hawaii island),
Maui
,
Lanai and Molokai
,
Kauai
, and
Oahu
. Go to those lists for detailed information on specific routes, including route numbers, names, termini, mileages, and sometimes historical or other information and/or links to photos and other material elsewhere on this site. Also on the left is a button for detailed guides to
Oahu Freeways
exits and interchanges, including interchange diagrams.
Click the dark blue buttons on the lower left for general information. The
site guide
discusses how this site is organized, supplementing the
site map
's quick overview of what's where on this site. The
FAQs
cover lots of Hawaii highway topics and trivia, including one page of "
Tips for Tourists
." See also my collection of
over 330 road photos covering all of Hawaii's major islands
, including in-depth coverage of some specific highways and topics, such as the
gorgeous Interstate H-3
, Maui's
curvaceous Hana Highway
, and
lava closures of highways on the Big Island
. There are also pages on
Hawaii road signs
,
Interstate route ends
, and
state and county route ends
. For the latest on state highway construction and traffic conditions, and other official information, check in also with
Hawaii DOT
.
The views expressed herein are not necessarily those of Hawaii's state or county transportation departments. However, they provided valuable
assistance (see
Credits and Sources
).
E komo mai!
(Come on in!)
Exit guides
General info
I want your kokua!
Any kokua (help) I can get from readers, to correct or update the information on this site, or to make it more informative or easier to use, would be greatly appreciated. I don't live in the islands, and don't get to visit as often as I'd like. While I try to keep up from afar with road-related news from the islands, those of you who live or travel there can help me keep this site up-to-date. Road photos, especially historical photos, to add to this site's road photos collection would also be welcome (see my "wish list" on the
overview page for the road photos collection
).
Please
e-mail me
with any corrections, updates, etc.
Mahalo nui loa!
(Thank you very much!)
See
my rant on why Hawaii should have a freeway (or at least a highway) named for the late Don Ho
.
© 1999-2010
Oscar Voss
. Material from original site © 1997-1999 C.C. Slater, used with his permission.
This site is non-profit, non-commercial, and has no advertising (if any ads pop up while viewing this site, they are coming from somewhere else).
Complete accuracy of the information on this site cannot be guaranteed. Also, this site provides only limited information on road hazards and other conditions, as explained in the
Site Guide
. For state highways, check in with
Hawaii DOT
for updates on road closures and other conditions. Also inquire locally before driving in unfamilar areas, especially on unpaved roads.
For more tropical road photos, see my
Puerto Rico road photos pages
.
My Hot Springs and Highways home page
(including roads sites for other states).

data.title: Klein Bottle Amazon Brand Hijacking (2021)
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amazon上的品牌劫持问题及其影响

不同观点：
• CliffStoll指出，他在Amazon美国的品牌劫持问题已解决，但在Amazon加拿大仍未解决，导致他无法在加拿大销售Klein瓶。他请求帮助解决此问题。
• sytelus认为Amazon对假冒伪劣产品问题漠不关心，中国供应商通过专业手段参与其中。他还提到其他竞争对手如Walmart和B&N在解决此类问题方面也不尽如人意。
• ColinWright介绍CliffStoll的身份和成就，提到CliffStoll的TED演讲及其作品《The Cuckoo's Egg》，并分享与其相处的经历，表达对其的赞赏。
• alister补充CliffStoll的身份背景，强调其在计算机 espionage 领域的贡献，并讨论Hacker News如何处理名人身份被冒用的问题。
• BrenBarn主张拆分大型企业如Amazon，认为市场份额过大导致企业对客户需求不再敏感，主张通过反垄断法律来解决。
• ggm提到监管缺失问题，指出Amazon等大企业似乎不受监管，呼吁Sherman反托拉斯法应对此类情况。
• iaw鼓励大家购买CliffStoll的Klein瓶，称其为宝藏。
• fermigier将CliffStoll的Klein瓶与Jacques Carelman的“Catalogue d'objets introuvables”相比较，强调其艺术和设计价值。
• b00ty4breakfast认为消费者对不便的容忍和消费习惯使Amazon得以继续其不良行为，呼吁通过伤害其业务来促使改变。
• AnotherGoodName认为像StockX这样提供验证服务的网站将超越Amazon，因为消费者更愿意为信任和无麻烦的购物体验支付更多。
• godelski担心如果不是像CliffStoll这样有名的人遇到此类问题，普通卖家将更难解决。
• neuroelectron分享了自己提交问题解决票但因无日志记录而关闭的经历。
• burnt-resistor赞赏CliffStoll的努力和产品质量，将其与Etsy卖家相比较。
• ilamont引用Amazon员工在Seller Central论坛上的回复，指出Amazon解决品牌劫持问题的复杂流程，卖家需“耗尽”多种自助选项才能触发实际调查。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到Amazon在处理品牌劫持和其他问题上的不足，以及卖家在解决这些问题时面临的困难。
• 对Amazon市场主导地位及其客户信任的下降也有较多讨论，部分评论者认为这是Amazon逐渐失去竞争优势的原因。
• 评论中也涉及对监管和反垄断措施的需求，以解决大企业的不当行为。

争议焦点：
• Amazon在处理品牌劫持和假冒产品问题上的效率和态度成为争议的焦点，卖家和消费者对其解决方案和响应速度不满。

data.title: Cross-Account and Cross-Region Backups with AWS Backup (and Friends)
data.author: terussell85
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在使用AWS Backup时遇到的一个问题：尽管AI可能声称AWS Backup支持跨账户和跨区域备份，但实际上AWS Backup并不支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份。文章指出，AWS Backup可以支持跨账户复制和跨区域复制，但无法同时实现两者，特别是在处理RDS、Aurora、DocumentDB和Neptune等数据库服务时。

作者强调，为了满足数据保护和灾难恢复的需求，同时实现跨账户和跨区域备份是必要的。跨区域备份可以防止未经授权的访问，而跨账户备份则可以在区域性灾难（如火山爆发）时保护数据。

尽管AWS Backup支持集中式备份计划，但目前仍无法同时实现跨账户和跨区域的备份。作者建议了一种临时解决方案，即使用AWS Lambda脚本在完成第一次复制后触发第二次复制，并删除第一次复制。最终，作者期望AWS未来能支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份，以简化实施过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS Backup及其在应对勒索软件等场景中的有效性与使用价值

不同观点：
• **time0ut的观点：**
   - 认为AWS Backup在应对勒索软件场景时不够成熟（"half baked"），尤其是在将现有应用栈恢复到恢复账户时，操作复杂且费力。
   - 提到了一家名为Arpio的公司，认为其服务可以补充AWS Backup的不足，能够复制更多内容，推荐其他公司考虑使用Arpio。
   - 声明自己与Arpio无利益关联，只是曾与客户合作使用过。

minutes
In today’s edition of “don’t trust LLMs”, we learn that despite what AI tells you, AWS Backup doesn’t support Cross-Account and Cross-Region backups. It supports Cross-Account copying and Cross-Region copying, but apparently
not together
.
As part of Masset’s Data Protection and Disaster Recovery policies, we determined that having backups separated by both region
and
OU account was a good idea. This follows fairly closely to AWS’s recommended best practice of using a separate, centralized account for an immutable history of backups and log. In the case of logging, this is a no-brainer. Most services require just a few simple tweaks to copy logs to a centralized location.
However, the story is a bit different for backups. AWS Backup’s lack of support for the combination of differing regions and account is unfortunate.  It’s a relatively new (in terms of AWS lifecycles) service offering, so I’m willing to give it a bit of leeway… But having to choose between region or account means we can only mitigate one risk at a time.
It all feels so simple; wit’s just a few lines of Terraform code. But the first time it runs you’ll get a failure notification in your #alerts Slack channel and you’ll see something akin this beautiful error hidden on the copy job for your backup.
It’s obviously not telling the
full
truth.
AWS clearly states in their documentation
that cross-region is allowed. Unfortunately, that little superscript #3 bears a lot of weight:
3. RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB, and Neptune do not support a single copy action that performs both cross-Region AND cross-account backup. You can choose one or the other. You can also use a AWS Lambda script to listen for the completion of your first copy, perform your second copy, then delete the first copy… See
Cross-Region copy considerations with specific resources
for further information.
Our risk profile demands both.
Cross-Region:
Being in a separate region doesn’t protect you if someone gets unauthorized access to your environment account. We want a WORM account for backups and logs.
Cross-Account:
Being in a separate account doesn’t protect if you’re running your application in
us-west-2
and the
Yellowstone Caldera decides to finally erupt
. Now you have data in a different account that also ceases to exist. To allow the few remaining remnants of society to pick up the pieces and restore your application to its full glory, moments before the eruption
1
, you also need your backups in a different region (preferably very far away from Wyoming).
So, what’s dev to do? Honestly, for the vast majority of organizations, having
any backup
is probably sufficient. So you might be best just to copy to a different account and call it good. Or copy it to a region in the same account. Either way, you’re probably fine according to whatever your Risk profile and matrix specifies. Talk to your compliance officer for more details.
But since ignoring the problem would make this article irrelevant, let’s continue forth as if we
really really
need this.
A Foreword on Centralized Backups Using AWS Backup
It’s important to point out that AWS Backup has expanded in recent years and
does support the idea of centralized Backup Plans managed through a delegated account in an organization
. In most cases, you should use that approach instead of defining the Backup Plan in each source account. Behind the scenes, the copy jobs all turn out to be the same, but the centralized model can lead to simpler setup if your organization is complex.
However, as of June 2025, the dual-copy (region+account) problem unfortunately still exists in either approach, distributed or centralized. If you use a centralized Backup Plan and account for your organization, source accounts still can’t copy RDS backups across region and account to the destination at the same time. This inevitably leads to defining copies of your Vault and Plan in your Backup account for each active region in your source accounts. Then you need to setup automated copies to ensure they reach another Vault in a different, isolate region. Not ideal by far.
It seems like the natural evolution of centralized plans is that AWS will eventually support cross-account and cross-region copies simultaneously. Once that’s possible, you’ll be able to define a backup plan once and have it applied universally across your entire organization. Until then, just expect there still to be a bit of nuance in implementation. In this example, we’re going to assume that both source and destination live in the same region as the principles are the same.
The First Copy
The first decision we need to make is to determine which copy do we want to do first. One can be automated with AWS Backup, the other needs to trigger based on an EventBridge event.

44333155.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在使用AWS Backup时遇到的一个问题：尽管AI可能声称AWS Backup支持跨账户和跨区域备份，但实际上AWS Backup并不支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份。文章指出，AWS Backup可以支持跨账户复制和跨区域复制，但无法同时实现两者，特别是在处理RDS、Aurora、DocumentDB和Neptune等数据库服务时。

作者强调，为了满足数据保护和灾难恢复的需求，同时实现跨账户和跨区域备份是必要的。跨区域备份可以防止未经授权的访问，而跨账户备份则可以在区域性灾难（如火山爆发）时保护数据。

尽管AWS Backup支持集中式备份计划，但目前仍无法同时实现跨账户和跨区域的备份。作者建议了一种临时解决方案，即使用AWS Lambda脚本在完成第一次复制后触发第二次复制，并删除第一次复制。最终，作者期望AWS未来能支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份，以简化实施过程。

主要讨论点：用户对Radio Garden这一全球广播收听平台的功能、使用体验和相关技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极体验与推荐**：
  - **jen729w**：分享了自己常听的日本Shonan Beach FM，并提到曾通过HomePod设置快捷指令收听。该用户喜欢将广播作为背景音，但提醒不同时区的听众可能体验不同，且周末会有较多谈话内容。
  - **Kozmik1**：多年使用Radio Garden，推荐点击地名获取更多电台，尤其是塞内加尔和几内亚比绍的音乐。还希望在微软飞行模拟2020中加入播放当地电台的功能，但对美国 localized ads 感到不满。
  - **BrandoElFollito**：通过Radio Garden收听不熟悉的语言，并结合Google街景和维基百科探索各地文化，认为这种偶然发现的过程非常美妙。
  - **geff82**：从小喜欢收听远方电台，对Radio Garden表示赞赏。

• **语言学习与实用性**：
  - **Duanemclemore**：利用Radio Garden进行语言学习，认为即使广告也是练习机会，特别是不熟悉的语言。

• **技术与实现**：
  - **pmontra**：认为Radio Garden是一个不错的应用，但在使用uMatrix时遇到困难，因为需要对特定电台的JS进行白名单处理，且大城市电台不固定。质疑是否能在服务器端解决此问题。
  - **phrotoma**：惊讶于Radio Garden的定位功能，未允许浏览器获取位置却能准确检测所在城市。

• **替代方案与扩展**：
  - **rcarmo**：提供了其他类似网站如Radio Paradise、Radiooooo、Music for Programming，尽管后者不算真正的广播。
  - **dunno7456**：提到Shoutcast目录仍然有效，并幽默地提到"whiping the llamas ass"。

• **技术问题与限制**：
  - **NoboruWataya**：遇到地域限制问题，尽管位于英国，却被提示"英国以外电台不可用"。

补充讨论：
• 部分用户提到广告体验不佳，特别是美国广告，并探讨了可能的解决方案，如自定义位置信息传递。
• 用户对Radio Garden的实现技术表示好奇，尤其是如何实现全球电台播放。
• 一些用户提供了其他收听全球电台的替代资源，扩展了讨论的范围。

data.title: Interview with Francine Prose on early-1970s San Francisco [audio]
data.author: keiferski
data.article_summary: 在这期播客中，主持人Donovan Hohn与作家Francine Prose对谈，探讨了她回忆中的旧金山，特别是在尼克松时代的经历。Prose描述了1970年代旧金山的群居生活和艺术家的自由创作环境，当时这座城市尚未被科技产业改变。她还分享了与五角大楼文件揭密者Tony Russo的关系，以及1960年代反主流文化的衰落。此外，他们讨论了Prose最喜欢的电影《迷魂记》（Vertigo）与当时社会氛围的共鸣。整个对话充满了对过去理想主义的怀念和对历史事件的反思。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对旧金山城市变化的看法，特别是与历史、文化、科技产业崛起相关的影响

不同观点：
• [tomhow] 认为音频内容在各大播客平台上都可以访问，回应了一些人关于页面无法访问的抱怨。他提供了多个平台的链接，但没有深入讨论旧金山本身的变化。

• [ipnon] 强调旧金山在不同历史时期的变迁，特别是从《在路上》一书中的描述对比当今城市的变化。他指出，尽管住房不稳定的问题依然存在，但像Dean Moriarty那样以零散工作维持家庭生活的可能性已经改变。他还提到Kevin Starr对加州历史的描述，并展望未来50年人们对旧金山的怀旧可能。

• [blululu] 认为该访谈标题有误导性，内容主要是年长者的闲聊，而很少真正谈论旧金山。他指出对旧金山的怀旧情绪，并通过引用电影《迷魂记》（Vertigo）来讨论这种怀旧和对过去的想象，认为旧金山一直被认为曾经更好。

• [blindriver] 作为科技工作者，批评科技产业的崛起对旧金山的负面影响。他怀念科技繁荣前的旧金山，认为科技工作者的大量涌入使得城市变得拥挤、昂贵且文化单一，失去了原有的多样性和活力。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于旧金山在不同历史阶段的文化和经济变化，特别是科技产业崛起对城市生活的显著影响。科技工作者和非科技工作者对这一变化的看法明显不同，前者中有人认为这种转变带来了负面影响，而后者则从历史角度分析城市变迁。
- 对旧金山怀旧情绪的讨论也是一个重要议题，部分评论者认为这种怀旧情绪忽视了过去的实际问题（如疾病和社会不稳定），而其他人则通过电影等文化作品来探讨这种情感。
- 音频内容的获取问题也在评论中被提及，但并非主要讨论点。

“I really loved it,”
Francine Prose
says of Nixon-era San Francisco in this episode of
The World in Time
, “but I also knew I wasn’t going to live there forever. Everyone I knew was living in these group houses in Berkeley, and then in the city itself, with ten people or fifteen people. I talk about the Reno Hotel, a former nineteenth-century hotel that had been built for boxers, and the city had given it to artists and designers and said,
You can live there, don’t burn it down
. And so they carved out these incredibly beautiful spaces for themselves. But this was before the tech revolution, when the Mission was still kind of wild and free, and it wasn’t all the glass cubes and people in tech. It was a great city to live in then. There was a kind of freedom there. Certainly compared to what I’d come from. My good fortune was that I wasn’t around a lot of hippies giving acid to two-year-olds. The book takes place during the Vietnam War. We went out and protested McNamara. My husband was the one who scaled the Pentagon, the walls of the Pentagon. We were very idealistic. Maybe unrealistically idealistic, but hey, I’ll take it.”
This week on the podcast, Donovan Hohn speaks with Francine Prose, author of
1974: A Personal History
, about the San Francisco she remembers from her youth, about her relationship with Pentagon Papers whistleblower Tony Russo, about the final defeat of 1960s counterculture, and about the eerie echoes of Prose’s favorite movie, Alfred Hitchcock’s
Vertigo
.

44349761.article_summary: 在这期播客中，主持人Donovan Hohn与作家Francine Prose对谈，探讨了她回忆中的旧金山，特别是在尼克松时代的经历。Prose描述了1970年代旧金山的群居生活和艺术家的自由创作环境，当时这座城市尚未被科技产业改变。她还分享了与五角大楼文件揭密者Tony Russo的关系，以及1960年代反主流文化的衰落。此外，他们讨论了Prose最喜欢的电影《迷魂记》（Vertigo）与当时社会氛围的共鸣。整个对话充满了对过去理想主义的怀念和对历史事件的反思。

• [tomhow] 认为音频内容在各大播客平台上都可以访问，回应了一些人关于页面无法访问的抱怨。他提供了多个平台的链接，但没有深入讨论旧金山本身的变化。

• [ipnon] 强调旧金山在不同历史时期的变迁，特别是从《在路上》一书中的描述对比当今城市的变化。他指出，尽管住房不稳定的问题依然存在，但像Dean Moriarty那样以零散工作维持家庭生活的可能性已经改变。他还提到Kevin Starr对加州历史的描述，并展望未来50年人们对旧金山的怀旧可能。

• [blululu] 认为该访谈标题有误导性，内容主要是年长者的闲聊，而很少真正谈论旧金山。他指出对旧金山的怀旧情绪，并通过引用电影《迷魂记》（Vertigo）来讨论这种怀旧和对过去的想象，认为旧金山一直被认为曾经更好。

• [blindriver] 作为科技工作者，批评科技产业的崛起对旧金山的负面影响。他怀念科技繁荣前的旧金山，认为科技工作者的大量涌入使得城市变得拥挤、昂贵且文化单一，失去了原有的多样性和活力。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于旧金山在不同历史阶段的文化和经济变化，特别是科技产业崛起对城市生活的显著影响。科技工作者和非科技工作者对这一变化的看法明显不同，前者中有人认为这种转变带来了负面影响，而后者则从历史角度分析城市变迁。
- 对旧金山怀旧情绪的讨论也是一个重要议题，部分评论者认为这种怀旧情绪忽视了过去的实际问题（如疾病和社会不稳定），而其他人则通过电影等文化作品来探讨这种情感。
- 音频内容的获取问题也在评论中被提及，但并非主要讨论点。

44350322.article_content:
I wrote my PhD Thesis in Typst
I recently submitted my
PhD thesis
, and while waiting for the physical copies to get printed I thought I'd write about something you (hopefully) wouldn't notice when reading it. I wrote it in Typst, not LaTeX. In this post I will talk a bit about what went well and what didn't.
Typst (
https://typst.app/
) is a modern take on a typesetting language that I think has a real shot at dethroning LaTeX. I would describe the language as a mix of markdown and dynamically typed Rust, which may sound weird but is a really nice fit. Day-to-day document writing being markdown-like is very comfortable (certainly much nicer than littering your writing with
\
). The scripting language is powerful, well thought out, and makes it very easy to jump between code and typesetting. For example
Produces
This is
bold text
. The sum of [1, 2, 5, 8] is
16
In the rest of this post, I will talk about some of the things I liked and disliked about Typst while writing the thesis.
The good
Compile times
The thing that pushed me over the edge to try Typst for my thesis was a friend telling me his LaTeX thesis took 90 seconds to compile towards the end. I am far too easily distracted to tolerate 90 second compile times when I'm making small changes. The Typst compiler is
fast
, on small-medium sized documents it compiles fast enough to do live writing in the PDF preview. As my thesis grew beyond 150 pages, compile times dropped a bit. Clean builds take about 15 seconds, but it also does incremental compilation so for
content
changes, it is still nearly instant, for local layout changes it takes a second or two. Even for large global template changes,  10 seconds is a whole lot better than 90 seconds, and I am confident that being able to iterate on layout and style 9 times faster produced a nicer looking result in the end.
The language
The Typst language is amazingly well thought out. Markdown syntax is nicer than Tex syntax for general writing, but what really shines is the scripting language. My biggest complaint with LaTeX as a language is that
nothing
is consistent. Every package defines their own little utilities for even basic things like
if
-statements. It feels like you don't learn LaTeX, you learn each package individually. Typst on the other hand is a well-designed dynamically typed language. Being Rust inspired and me being a Rust user meant that it barely feels like I had to learn the language at all, I can just assume that I'm writing Rust. That's not true as you get into more advanced things of course, but it feels like I
know
Typst in a way that I don't think is possible with LaTeX.
This isn't just philosophical, being able to script Typst is extremely useful. For example, a central part of my thesis is that there are a lot of hardware description languages out there, and I wanted to come up with a way to categorize them. Over a few years, I have collected them all with some metadata in a toml file (
https://gitlab.com/TheZoq2/list_of_hdls/
). Since Typst can parse toml, I could simply use that data to generate a figure to put the languages into my taxonomy:
Sure, it would be possible to do this in many other ways, but having it self-contained in the document is nice, and at this point Typst is one of my favourite scripting languages, so using it here is a no-brainer and something I did for pretty much all my data processing.
A modern language of course also comes with modern tools, a compiler with dependency management, a working language server protocol integration for editors etc. All that makes it even nicer to work with.
Layout Tweaks
A few times I have tried to understand latex templates, and every time it has ended in frustration. I believe it took me longer to remove a header from our university presentation template than it did for me to write a new presentation template in Typst. Again, this comes down to the language being well-thought-out and consistent. This was also hugely advantageous when tweaking my thesis template the way I want it. Naturally, this is something of a double-edged sword, had I used LaTeX I would not have had to make a template in the first place, but at the same time, modifying anything in that template would have been much more difficult. This way I ended up with everything right where I wanted it without the frustration of figuring out how to get the results I wanted.
Syntax Highlighting
My thesis has a lot of code in it, and I
hate
reading code without good syntax highlighting. LaTeX's syntax highlighting systems leave a lot to be desired, but Typst's certainly does not. It does have built in support for textmate grammars, the same system used by sublime text for syntax highlighting, but for various reasons I decided not to use them. Instead, I just used Typst's
show
rules with regex. For example,
will syntax highlight Spade conditionals. My syntax highlighting definitions¹ are… more more complicated but produce results that I am very happy with. At some poin

data.title: Using Home Assistant, adguard home and an $8 smart outlet to avoid brain rot
data.author: remuskaos
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过物理按钮控制互联网访问以减少社交媒体分心的方法。作者作为软件开发者，意识到互联网的必要性，但同时深受其广告、分心内容和社交媒体的困扰。为了解决这一问题，作者借鉴了Neil Chen的创意，利用智能插座和家庭自动化系统（Home Assistant）结合路由器的Adguard Home功能，实现按下按钮后允许访问社交媒体15分钟，随后进入1小时的冷却期。文章详细描述了设置Adguard Home自定义规则、API访问配置、Home Assistant集成及自动化配置的具体步骤，最终实现对网络访问的有效控制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同方法和工具解决手机成瘾及智能家居设备的选择与安全问题

不同观点：
• **手机成瘾测试方法**：AdieuToLogic提出了一系列逐步增加难度的练习，帮助人们检测自己是否对手机上瘾。这些练习包括在不使用手机的情况下度过一天，或者将手机留在家中以检测依赖程度。
• **复杂系统的价值**：userbinator认为设计复杂的系统来解决分心问题是一种过度工程化，可能只是为了满足某种技术社区的偏好。
• **技术工具的应用**：
  ◦ tmhrtly推荐了OneSec应用，通过引入时间延迟和任务来减少无意识的手机使用，但指出该应用需要访问私人浏览数据。
  ◦ ricardobeat和varenc讨论了在网络层面阻止网站的技术困难，指出浏览器和手机使用硬编码的DNS解析器，使得这种方法的效用有限。
  ◦ varenc分享了使用Alfred在Mac上通过快捷键改变DNS设置的方法，这种方法只影响个人设备而不干扰整个网络。
• **智能家居的安全与设置**：
  ◦ polivier分享了使用Home Assistant和各种传感器保护家庭安全的经验，强调了不依赖单一应用或生态系统的优势。
  ◦ gerdesj强调了智能家居设备的选择标准，包括主电源供电、在WiFi/以太网中断时仍能工作，以及对互联网访问的严格控制。
  ◦ suprjami推荐了GL-iNet路由器，指出其兼容OpenWrt的优点。
• **技术反制措施的讨论**：
  ◦ remuskao和FrankPetrilli提到使用AdGuard和Home Assistant自动化来暂时禁用网络过滤器或关闭设备，以应对社交媒体成瘾问题。
  ◦ urbandw311er认为反制措施需要更难逆转，以避免轻易绕过。

补充讨论：
• **NextDNS的应用**：jz10提到NextDNS的隐私和家长控制功能表现出色，提供了一种有效的网络内容控制方案。
• **个人经验和建议**：weq分享了通过关闭通知和培养爱好来减少对社交媒体依赖的经验，认为这些方法有助于打破对技术的过度依赖。

争议焦点：
• 针对手机成瘾的技术解决方案的有效性和复杂性。userbinator质疑通过设计复杂系统来解决分心问题的必要性，而其他人如tmhrtly和ricardobeat则分享了具体的工具和方法。

44350002.article_content:
Beating Brainrot by Button
2025-06-22
What an effort to turn of the internet.
Preamble
#
The internet is the bane of my existence. Ads, distractions, sponsored content, bad news, bad ideas, more ads, social media, antisocial media, even more ads.
Also, I’m a software developer, so the internet is basically indispensable for me, a central pillar of my income and a convenient way to communicate with friends, family, loved ones, associates, acquaintances, people from my sports club, superpositions of all previous groups and enemies alike. And I think my company runs ads, so in a way ads pay for my clothing and food and stuff. So I guess my current stance towards the internet would be somewhat neutral-ish, but that may still change.
But I can try to reduce or at least moderate some of the negative aspects of the internet, especially those that keep me hooked like some sad addict: social media. I’ve tried completely blocking it via my networks’ ad blocker, but the animal in me circumvented that blockage by turning off wifi on the cell phone and thus doom scrolling galore on my cell plan. Also, my wife needs some social media for work or research (and of course guilty pleasure) at least some of the time, but she’s as bad in moderation as me. So completely blocking is not viable, but allowing unrestricted internet access to two reasonable adults is somehow also out of the question.
So the problem remained mathematically unsolvable.
Until today, when
Neil Chen posted a simply genius idea to hacker news
. Neil describes how a smart plug is used to dynamically rewrite some ublock Origin lists to allow unfetted access to all content distracting. The idea is fantastic, but the implementation not practical for my/our scenario, so I’m adapting it here.
Building Blocks
#
I’m already using an network wide ad blocker via my gli.net router called “Adblock Home”. And for a smart home without internet access (see preamble) I’m using Home Assistant.
So we have:
A gli.net router with Adguard Home
Home Assistant
Copious amounts of Zigbee Switches
Some spare time
Surely there must be some way to wire those together haywire-ly.
The Plan
#
Just like Neil, I want some button to press to allow for access to social media, but only for a limited time (say 15 minutes). After that time has passed, my wife and me must endure a cool-down phase until we can push the button again (say one hour). So whenever we push the button, the filters will be disabled for 15 sin-filled minutes. A Zigbee enabled smart plug is adequately suited.
Setting Up Adguard Home on the gli.net Router
#
Adguard Home is very conveniently integrated into gli.net’s fork/customization of OpenWRT (formerly Lede, formerly OpenWRT). Frst, we set up the services we wish to block as custom rules. Sadly we cannot use the built-in services, because they don’t seem to count as “custom” and thus cannot be toggled on and off.
API Access to Adguard Home
#
Adguard Home has a fantastic API, available in OpenAPI yaml. You login to that API with the normal user and password. But: The routers main interface somehow bypasses the authentication, which means Adguard Home has no user/password which we could use for API access.
This forum link
explains how one can be added without breaking the existing integration. Basically, we have to add them by hand to the
/etc/Adguard/config.yaml
file. Change:
users
: []
to
users
:
-
name
:
admin
password
:
$2a$10$dXh72ZnexWPjxzRumXX2fOU2gwvPzqM8OZmcWZmFYl1WEiyhOMj2u
This password is the bcrypt hash of
admin
, but of course thats not the password I’m actually using.
Use cyberchef to generate the hash
.
Home Assistant Integration
#
Home Assistant comes with a functional, but somewhat reduced integration. It can however do all we need.
Among the switches it exposes is “Filtering”, which enables or disables application of custom filter rules. We can flick this switch via automation.
The Home Assistant Automation
#
After some trial and error, I’ve arrived at this automation, which as of now seems to work just fine and just like I intended.

44350002.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过物理按钮控制互联网访问以减少社交媒体分心的方法。作者作为软件开发者，意识到互联网的必要性，但同时深受其广告、分心内容和社交媒体的困扰。为了解决这一问题，作者借鉴了Neil Chen的创意，利用智能插座和家庭自动化系统（Home Assistant）结合路由器的Adguard Home功能，实现按下按钮后允许访问社交媒体15分钟，随后进入1小时的冷却期。文章详细描述了设置Adguard Home自定义规则、API访问配置、Home Assistant集成及自动化配置的具体步骤，最终实现对网络访问的有效控制。
44350002.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **手机成瘾测试方法**：AdieuToLogic提出了一系列逐步增加难度的练习，帮助人们检测自己是否对手机上瘾。这些练习包括在不使用手机的情况下度过一天，或者将手机留在家中以检测依赖程度。
• **复杂系统的价值**：userbinator认为设计复杂的系统来解决分心问题是一种过度工程化，可能只是为了满足某种技术社区的偏好。
• **技术工具的应用**：
  ◦ tmhrtly推荐了OneSec应用，通过引入时间延迟和任务来减少无意识的手机使用，但指出该应用需要访问私人浏览数据。
  ◦ ricardobeat和varenc讨论了在网络层面阻止网站的技术困难，指出浏览器和手机使用硬编码的DNS解析器，使得这种方法的效用有限。
  ◦ varenc分享了使用Alfred在Mac上通过快捷键改变DNS设置的方法，这种方法只影响个人设备而不干扰整个网络。
• **智能家居的安全与设置**：
  ◦ polivier分享了使用Home Assistant和各种传感器保护家庭安全的经验，强调了不依赖单一应用或生态系统的优势。
  ◦ gerdesj强调了智能家居设备的选择标准，包括主电源供电、在WiFi/以太网中断时仍能工作，以及对互联网访问的严格控制。
  ◦ suprjami推荐了GL-iNet路由器，指出其兼容OpenWrt的优点。

  ◦ remuskao和FrankPetrilli提到使用AdGuard和Home Assistant自动化来暂时禁用网络过滤器或关闭设备，以应对社交媒体成瘾问题。

补充讨论：
